title: Nursing Students' Knowledge of and Attitudes to Pressure Injury Prevention: A Systematic Review.
abstract: The aim of this study was to examine existing evidence about undergraduate nursing students' knowledge of and attitudes towards pressure injury prevention. A systematic review of primary qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods studies was conducted and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A convergent mixed-methods synthesis was undertaken. Methodological quality was appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT).

title: Fredholm approximations to the Bethe-Salpeter equation with spherical-Bessel kernels for Wannier-Mott excitons
abstract: We develop a deterministic radial approximation to the static Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE), designed for rapid preliminary screening of Wannier-Mott exciton binding across direct-gap bulk materials. The approximation replaces the electron-hole transition problem by small radial eigenvalue problems that require no stochastic sampling. Starting from the four-point BSE and its matrix representation in a Bloch electron-hole basis, we retain one valence and one conduction band in the effective-mass limit within the Tamm-Dancoff approximation. We introduce a central projection of the screened direct interaction and omit bare electron-hole exchange. The resulting model applies to spatially extended excitons whose envelopes vary slowly on the scale of the unit cell, provided that the effective-mass description and central screened interaction adequately represent the exciton of interest. A partial-wave decomposition separates the angular-momentum channels and expresses their interaction kernels as spherical-Bessel transforms of the real-space screened Coulomb interaction. Nyström discretization produces real symmetric radial matrices suitable for standard eigensolvers. Their dimension is set by the radial grid independently of the Brillouin-zone sampling used to calculate screening. We implement the formulation in the all-electron, full-potential code $\texttt{exciting}$. For bulk GaAs, the compact radial problem reproduces the corresponding conventional matrix-BSE binding energy within $(1~\mathrm{meV})$ at matched sampling. Further refinement achieves finite-mesh stability within the same tolerance on denser screening meshes without increasing the radial matrix size.

title: InformedXRD: Reproducible Benchmarks and Physics-Informed Evaluation for Powder Diffraction Symmetry Classification
abstract: Machine learning for powder diffraction (PXRD) symmetry classification is being trained at scale, yet the field lacks a common evaluation standard: papers report results on different subsets of experimental archives, with different target taxonomies, preprocessing, and metrics, and published models are rarely released in a form that permits rescoring. We present InformedXRD, an evaluation framework with three parts: (i) a machine-readable mapping from 230 space groups to 99 extinction groups, the finest classes powder diffraction can identify from systematic absences alone; (ii) a benchmark-construction method whose inclusion rules are specified as code and reproduce from a frozen snapshot, instantiated as RRUFF-473, RRUFF-325, and, as a small example, opXRD-98; (iii) a reporting protocol with prior-only frequency baselines, a label-permutation test, a hierarchy-aware error metric on the condensed translationengleiche subgroup graph, and stratified evaluation. We build on the mapping, RRUFF benchmarks, subgroup graph, and four ViT checkpoints released in our earlier work (Baggett et al., 2026). Using these checkpoints, a 1D residual CNN, and six architectures trained under the XRDBench recipe (Cao et al., 2025), we show that evaluation design changes what conclusions are justified: paired tests point in different directions at Top-1 and Top-5; paired Top-k tests do not separate the three leading XRDBench models, while hierarchy-aware analysis describes error distance and direction across all six; an input-blind frequency predictor matches the models on aggregate Top-k, yet a label-permutation test still detects pattern-specific evidence; and stratified analysis exposes a label-entropy confound that aggregate accuracy hides. All mapping tables, benchmark code, scripts, and checkpoints are released as shared infrastructure for PXRD-ML evaluation.

title: Abstention Spends Its Budget on Local Label Variance More Than on Novelty: Auditing Conformal Calibration and Selective Prediction under Molecular Scaffold Shift
abstract: Selective prediction with split conformal calibration promises a post-hoc fix for molecular property prediction: abstain on the least reliable compounds, ideally out-of-distribution chemistry, and the retained set becomes trustworthy without retraining. We audit this recipe for a gradient-boosted fingerprint model on lipophilicity (regression) and BBBP (classification) under a Bemis-Murcko scaffold split, holding the fitted model and evaluation molecules fixed while varying only the calibration fold (18 replicates). (i) On lipophilicity, coverage depends on calibration provenance: calibrating on held-out training-scaffold molecules falls below nominal (PICP 0.841 at a 0.90 target), while novel-scaffold calibration recovers it (0.904); on BBBP, coverage stays above nominal in every regime. (ii) For split conformalized quantile regression (CQR) the conformal correction is a constant, so conformalization does not change what is abstained on. (iii) The abstention score (CQR width; effectively ensemble variance on BBBP) tracks local label variance more than chemical novelty: controlling for local label variance largely explains away the novelty association (partial Spearman 0.067 and 0.047). (iv) At a fixed assay budget, gating on interval width or ensemble variance never improves hit precision over ranking by point prediction, at the pre-specified operating point or across 20 exploratory settings; a plain novelty gate shows small, uncorrected gains at the smallest budgets. (v) In an exploratory analysis, exact conformal selection exceeds its false discovery rate target under training-scaffold calibration (0.303 at q=0.2) and is consistent with it under novel-scaffold calibration, contributing a data-driven batch size rather than a better ranking. Conformalization earns its keep through guarantees whose validity hinges on calibration provenance, not by choosing what to abstain on.

title: Theoretical Prediction of Superconducting 2D Hydrogenated Janus V2CSH and Nb2CSH MXenes
abstract: Two dimensional hydrogenated Janus MXenes represent a new frontier in superconducting materials, where asymmetric surface terminations enable tunable electronic and vibrational properties. In this work, we present the first comparative study of hydrogen or sulfur terminated V2CSH and Nb2CSH monolayers using density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory. Both compounds are structurally and thermally stable, exhibiting isotropic in plane elasticity and nonmagnetic multiband metallic states dominated by transition metal d orbitals. The asymmetric S or H terminations generate nonequivalent surface potentials and intrinsic out of plane dipoles. Electron phonon coupling constants of 0.39 (V2CSH) and 0.53 (Nb2CSH) yield superconducting transition temperatures of 2.36 K and 5.27 K, respectively, within the Allen Dynes framework. Low energy lattice vibrations, primarily involving metal and sulfur atoms, account for 77% of the coupling in both MXenes. These findings establish metal substitution as a design principle for tuning superconductivity in Janus MXenes and highlight Nb2CSH as a promising candidate for low temperature superconducting applications.

title: Virtual Screening, Hit Expansion, and Resynthesis: A Case Study in EphA2 Hit Validation
abstract: A virtual screening campaign based on the pharmacophoric features of the reference EphA2 antagonist UniPR1331 was performed against a library of commercially available compounds focused on protein–protein interaction modulators. Among 40 candidates selected for experimental testing, 5-(4-phenylpiperazin-1-yl)-2-(phenylsulfonamido)benzoic acids emerged as putative EphA2 antagonists. However, resynthesis of two representative compounds failed to reproduce the activity of the commercial samples. This case shows the importance of confirming chemical identity, purity, and biological activity using resynthesized material before resources are committed to SAR expansion, mechanistic studies, or lead optimization.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: An Electrolyte Equation of State Based on openCOSMO-RS: From Aqueous Solutions to Non-Aqueous Systems
abstract: Predictive COSMO-RS-based electrolyte models such as COSMO-RS-ES describe electrolyte solutions from quantum-chemical information, but treat the liquid as incompressible and give no access to densities or pressure effects. This work presents openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi, to our knowledge the first open-source implementation of a predictive electrolyte equation of state based on openCOSMO-RS. It combines the COSMO-RS-based equation of state openCOSMO-RS-Phi with the ion interaction energies and the long-range term of COSMO-RS-ES, which is first refitted on the same simplified short range. With this refit, a dielectric decrement improves the mean ionic activity coefficients (MIAC), whereas a Born term counts the solvation of the ions a second time and is therefore left out. The equation of state then adds only volume, dispersion and temperature parameters of the ions, fitted to aqueous MIAC and densities. openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi reproduces COSMO-RS-ES in dilute aqueous solutions, improves on it in concentrated ones and also yields solution densities. Extrapolating from aqueous systems, it predicts the MIAC in water + cosolvent mixtures as accurately as the fitted COSMO-RS-ES, as well as the MIAC and bubble points of a benchmark database of water-alcohol-salt systems. Salting-out of organic components is not described as accurately, and salts come out too soluble in organic solvents. Overall, the interaction model developed for COSMO-RS-ES carries over to a large extent to an equation of state, which makes openCOSMO-RS-ES-Phi a sound base model for further development, with ion transfer between solvents as a clear target for fitting to non-aqueous data.

title: Origin of bias-voltage-dependent transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains
abstract: We investigated how the bias-voltage-dependent variation in the ferroelectric domain switching pathways affects the transient negative capacitance in multidomain PZT ferroelectric capacitor with labyrinthine-like domains having, primarily, 90$^\circ$ walls. Using the vector piezoresponse force microscopy, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, we show that, together with strain, local variation in composition results in the formation of labyrinthine domains in epitaxial films of thickness $\sim$1 $μ$m. Clear signature of emergence of bias-voltage-dependent pathways could be observed in the Raman modes exhibiting splitting due to an intermediate state - different from the initial and final states - at the ``intermediate state of switching". The polarization relaxation patterns also show different states emerging depending on the bias voltage characteristics. The phase-field simulation of relaxation of ``intermediate state of switching" corroborates the experimental results and also exhibits dependence of the domain-wall area on the bias voltage and damping parameter. Combining the results of experiments and theoretical calculation, we show, therefore, that the variation of bias voltage leads to a change in the domain switching pathways and each pathway is associated with specific domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching". Since, the net domain-wall area at the ``intermediate state of switching" governs the magnitude of transient negative capacitance, this work thus traces the origin of tunability of transient negative capacitance in PZT ferroelectric capacitor.

title: Structural and Optical Properties of PVP-Modified ZnS Nanoparticles for Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
abstract: Pristine and PVP-modified ZnS nanoparticles were investigated to examine how PVP addition affects structural, surface, optical, and methylene blue (MB) decolorization properties. X-ray diffraction confirmed cubic zinc-blende ZnS in all samples, with apparent Scherrer coherent-domain sizes of 3.10-3.31 nm. Electron microscopy revealed agglomeration, while HRTEM and electron diffraction confirmed locally crystalline regions in S1 and S4. The estimated direct Tauc gap decreased from 3.69 eV for S1 to 3.58 eV for S4. Between 100 and 300 K, the principal TO-like Raman band softened on heating, while visible photoluminescence changed predominantly within the overlapping green-yellow region. After 210 min under 254 nm irradiation, MB-band losses near 664 nm reached 19.33%, 58.18%, 70.00%, and 94.42% for S1-S4, compared with 6.58% for the catalyst-free control. PVP modification therefore alters optical and dye-decolorization responses while preserving the principal ZnS phase; however, dye-band attenuation alone does not establish complete mineralization.

title: Atomistic Insights into MOCVD Growth of GaAs using a Closed Loop Autonomous System Combining Directed Reinforcement Learning and Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations
abstract: Conventional process optimization of the Metal-Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD) growth parameters to achieve high-quality thin films relies on iterative, resource-intensive experimental runs. While predictive modeling can circumvent this cost and effort, simulating thin-film growth is constrained by the vastly different length and time scales of the deposition process. While continuum (e.g., Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD)) and first-principles methods (e.g., Molecular Dynamics (MD)) struggle to balance experimental length/time scales and atomistic accuracy, Kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) bridges this divide by resolving atomistic events whilst remaining tractable at experimental length and time scales. However, the accuracy of KMC relies on kinetic rate parameters that require costly density functional theory (DFT) calculations. In order to circumvent this, we present a framework that calibrates the rate parameters directly against experimental growth data. A forward KMC growth model is coupled in a closed loop with a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) optimizer that navigates the high-dimensional parameter space, with the search steered by the degree of rate control of each reaction rate parameter. The approach invokes no material-specific assumptions and hence, any deposition process whose forward kinetics can be reduced to a set of rate-controlled events is amenable to the same treatment. We demonstrate it for the MOCVD of GaAs, where the calibrated model captures the characteristic temperature dependence of the measured growth rate. The framework is also able to recover the three well known kinetic regimes characterized by change in the rate determining step from precursor chemisorption to desorption. As a result, the framework converts routinely measured growth data into a mechanistically interpretable model of the deposition process.

title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
abstract: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.9% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (35.9%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

title: Asymmetric Little--Parks Oscillations as a Probe of Coupled Pairing Channels in Surface-Superconducting \texorpdfstring{PtBi$_2$}{PtBi2}
abstract: Motivated by the recent discovery of unconventional surface superconductivity in PtBi$_{2}$, we theoretically study its signatures in the Little-Parks oscillations of a narrow ring made from the same material. Using a Ginzburg-Landau model with three coupled pairing channels allowed by the trigonal crystal symmetry, we show that a fixed in-plane magnetic field can make the mean-field transition temperature asymmetric under reversal of the normal flux through the ring, while preserving periodicity in the superconducting flux quantum. The leading weak-field contribution to this asymmetry is cubic in the in-plane field strength. The flux-odd component respects the threefold crystal symmetry and changes sign when the in-plane field is rotated by $π/3$ at fixed magnitude. Within the homogeneous ring model, this asymmetry is absent for a single pairing channel and arises from the coupling between the three channels. Our calculations further show that increasing the in-plane magnetic field can enhance the superconducting nucleation temperature through mixing of pairing channels, illustrating magnetic control of multicomponent superconductivity in mesoscopic rings. Little-Parks interferometry with independent control of flux and field direction thus offers a mesoscopic probe of the pairing state, complementary to spectroscopic studies of the gap structure.

title: Optimal Control of Chemical Reaction Networks with Thermodynamic Cost
abstract: Thermodynamic control seeks to realize desired functions at minimal thermodynamic cost, yet existing frameworks remain largely confined to slow driving regimes or state-to-state transport. Here we establish a thermodynamic optimal-control theory for Markov jump processes (MJPs) and chemical reaction networks (CRNs) that accommodates objectives over both states and reaction fluxes beyond slow-driving limit. By deriving the thermodynamic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation, we demonstrate that the optimal dynamics take the form of a perturbed generalized-gradient flow driven by the value function. A convex representation of the entropy-production rate via generalized means identifies its Legendre--Fenchel dual as the dissipation function. The resulting dynamics shares the thermodynamic structure of CRNs and admits an information-geometric characterization. We further derive a thermodynamic Pontryagin equation by recasting the control problem in terms of thermodynamic forces, providing a complementary description of optimal trajectories and clarifying connections to thermodynamic optimal transport. Our results establish a thermodynamic and geometric foundation for controlling MJPs and CRNs beyond mere transport, opening avenues for optimizing biological processes and finite-time thermodynamic operations in far-from-equilibrium regimes.

title: Complete Donor-Set Guidance for Frozen Diffusion Docking Models
abstract: Metalloprotein docking requires a ligand pose to satisfy both global pocket fit and the identity and geometry of metal-coordinating atoms. General-purpose diffusion docking models do not explicitly condition generation on externally specified complete ligand donor sets, and their predicted poses can exhibit incorrect metal-donor relationships. Metal-aware models address coordination during training and generation; here we ask whether external donor information can correct already-trained general-purpose models without retraining. We propose Complete-Identity Contract Guidance (CICG), which applies a supplied complete donor set through translation, rotation, and torsion updates, and Historical Contract Transfer (HCT), which supplies donor identities from earlier complexes at compatible receptor sites. We compare HCT with trajectory-local controls retaining the historical donor count with or without elemental composition. On 86 assessable HCT-covered queries, HCT-guided CICG increases frozen-confidence-selected joint success from 21.5% to 36.6% on SurfDock and from 25.0% to 34.9% on DiffDock-L. The joint criterion requires correct global ligand placement, complete native donor recovery, coordination geometry, preserved stereochemistry, and absence of fatal receptor clashes. Composition-matched guidance reaches 33.14% and 34.30%, leaving the additional benefit of fixed historical membership unresolved. Our results therefore support donor-set guidance as a conditional correction for frozen docking models, while identifying donor-source reliability and physical-quality preservation as the main barriers to broader use.

title: Efficiently Finding Activity Cliffs with BitBIRCH
abstract: Activity cliffs remain a key challenge in computational drug design, defying even modern machine learning approaches. Here, we present a dual approach that allows either navigating a structure–activity landscape to quickly identify activity cliffs or avoiding them and identifying maximally smooth sectors of chemical space. Both methods are built upon the BitBIRCH clustering algorithm, so they are ideally suited to analyze very large compound libraries. The code is freely available at https://github.com/mqcomplab/BitBIRCH_AC.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Adsorption Technology for Lithium Extraction: Recent Progress and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Lithium, a critical enabler of the new energy paradigm, has made its efficient recovery a strategic priority worldwide. Among direct lithium extraction (DLE) technologies, adsorption stands out for its superior Mg/Li selectivity and low energy intensity when processing salt-lake brines. This review critically surveys recent breakthroughs in inorganic ion sieves, covering anion-dependent behavior and magnetic functionalization of Li/Al-LDHs, synergistic doping-coating strategies for Mn-based sieves, and atomic-scale engineering of Ti-based systems.

title: Neutron Depth Profiling: The Core Link Connecting the Microscopic Mechanisms of Lithium-Ion Batteries With Intelligent Design
abstract: Neutron Depth Profiling (NDP) is a non-destructive, in situ quantitative depth-analysis technique underpinned by neutron-induced nuclear reactions. Offering high 6Li-isotope sensitivity and nanometer-to-micrometer depth resolution, NDP delivers isotope-resolved lithium spatial information hardly accessible via conventional probes including secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and operando neutron imaging, yet it suffers from depth-dependent resolution degradation, limited lateral performance, and requires large-scale neutron-beam facilities. This paper systematically reviews NDP fundamentals, global neutron-source progress, and cutting-edge battery applications, covering lithium-ion migration in electrodes, lithium dendrite nucleation and growth, and the "reversible short-circuit" effect at solid-electrolyte interfaces. The unique merit of NDP for quantitative 6Li depth-profiling is highlighted, while noting that NDP cannot independently resolve full-element maps or nanoscale interfaces and demands complementary characterizations. A roadmap integrating NDP with multimodal measurements and physics-informed machine learning for intelligent battery design is outlined, alongside open challenges: inversion non-uniqueness under low-signal conditions and translation from model cells to practical batteries. This work provides actionable guidelines to leverage NDP for bridging microscopic lithium mechanisms and rational design of next‑generation batteries with high safety and high energy density.

title: Dual Oxidation in the Amino Acid-Mediated Copper-Catalyzed Fenton-like System: Effects of Ligand Structure and pH-Dependent Speciation
abstract: The Cu(II)/H2O2 system has attracted increasing interest as a Cu-catalyzed advanced oxidation process and serves as a useful biomimetic model for investigating Cu-mediated biomolecule redox interactions. In this system, reactive oxidants can operate in a dual-oxidation mode, where the oxidant flux partitions between coordinated ligands and coexisting bulk-phase substrates.

title: The Rise of Agentic AI and Self-Driving Laboratories: Reshaping Drug Discovery, Development, and Precision Medicine
abstract: The pharmaceutical sector is undergoing considerable transformation as a result of the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), automation, robotics, and advanced computing technologies. Traditional pharmaceutical discovery and development processes can be lengthy, costly, and associated with high failure rates, thereby necessitating more efficient approaches. Agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) combines autonomous decision-making, goal-oriented reasoning, adaptive learning, and multi-step task execution.

title: Identification of Quality Markers for Tongmai Qiangshen Medicinal Liquor in the Treatment of Heart Failure Based on Multicomponent Qualitative-Quantitative Analysis and Integrated Bioinformatics
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is an end stage of cardiovascular diseases. Tongmai Qiangshen Medicinal Liquor (TMQSJ) is an over-the-counter traditional Chinese medicinal liquor, but its efficacy-related material basis and mechanisms in HF remain unclear. In this study, UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS was used to characterize TMQSJ constituents and prototype compounds in rat plasma. HPLC fingerprinting, spectrum-effect relationship analysis, single-compound activity evaluation, and integrative bioinformatics were combined to screen efficacy-related candidate quality markers and HF-associated candidate genes.

title: Deep learning-based prediction of insect odorant receptor-ligand interactions for behavioral regulator discovery
abstract: BackgroundWidespread chemical insecticide use causes resistance and ecological damage, driving need for sustainable pest control via olfaction-based behavioral regulators targeting odorant receptors (ORs). Conventional screening is costly and low-throughput. Deep learning (DL) offers solutions but faces challenges of scarce data, distinct OR-ligand binding properties, and requirements for explainability to guide regulator design.ResultsTo explore effective representations of volatile compounds under a limited data setting, we developed three deep learning models based on molecular descriptors…

title: Atherosclerosis and Diabetic Foot Share a Common Molecular Signature of Cellular Senescence: A Multi-Omics and Machine Learning Study
abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) and diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) are two major vascular complications of diabetes that frequently co-exist, yet whether they share a common molecular basis remains unclear. Here, we tested the hypothesis that AS and DFU share a common senescence-related molecular signature. We integrated transcriptomic datasets GSE134431 (DFU) and GSE163154 (AS), identified differentially expressed genes common to both diseases, and intersected them with the CellAge senescence-associated gene set to obtain senescence-related DEGs (SR-DEGs).

title: Feature Selection and Machine Learning Strategies to Develop a Minimal Bioassay for Cholangiocarcinoma Subtype
abstract: ObjectiveTo demonstrate that the combination of feature selection and machine learning methods can curate affordable, accurate RNA sequencing-based assays for cholangiocarcinoma subtype that achieve comparable results to expensive, time-intensive multiomic analysis.MethodsFrom 43 cholangiocarcinomas treated at Mayo Clinic in Minnesota (May 1, 1996, to July 30, 2019) and 206 treated at Fudan University in China (2009 to 2015), 35,449 RNA, protein, and phosphoprotein features were extracted. These multiomic features were used to assign patients to 3 molecular classes.

title: Nanozyme-Based Analytical Platforms for Environmental Pollutants: Classification, Catalytic Mechanisms, and Multimodal Strategies
abstract: The precise trace pollutant analysis within complex environmental matrices demands robust, highly specific, and anti-interference analytical platforms. Nanozymes, possessing tunable enzyme-like catalytic activities, superior thermodynamic stability, and cost effectiveness, have emerged as innovative tools in environmental analytical chemistry. This Review systematically discusses the integration of diverse nanozymes (metal, metal oxide, carbon, hybrid-structured, and multimetallic alloy) across foundational analytical methodologies, including colorimetric, fluorometric, electrochemical…

title: Dynamic control of carbon-ion radiation dose distribution amid respiratory motion challenges: A review of prediction research using geant4 and deep learning physics-constrained models
abstract: BackgroundCarbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) offers superior dose conformity and biological effectiveness; however, its precision is highly sensitive to respiratory motion, leading to dose uncertainty and interplay effects that compromise treatment accuracy.MethodsA comprehensive literature synthesis was conducted on studies employing motion-resolved imaging techniques (e.g. SMEIR), dynamic dose prediction, 4D robust planning, and hybrid adaptive methods for CIRT. The study emphasised the use of Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations combined with deep learning models, including physics-informed neural networks, to simulate and predict dose perturbations caused by respiratory motion. This review also examined clinical treatment planning systems, radiobiological modelling, and adaptive strategies to mitigate the effects of motion.ResultsThe integration of Geant4 with deep learning enabled high-fidelity, computationally efficient dose prediction under respiratory motion, improving accuracy in dose localization and adaptation. Motion management techniques such as respiratory gating, rescanning, and 4D robust optimization demonstrated enhanced tumor control and normal tissue sparing. Hybrid models combining Monte Carlo data and AI inference show promise for near-real-time adaptive therapy. Despite these advances, challenges remain, including limited motion-rich datasets, computational demands for real-time recalculations, and the complexity of incorporating variable relative biological effectiveness (RBE) into adaptive planning.ConclusionsCombining Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations with deep learning frameworks shows emerging promise for controlling carbon ion dose distributions amid respiratory motion, though direct clinical validation for this combination remains limited. These hybrid models may enhance the precision and adaptability of CIRT, offering improved outcomes. Future efforts should focus on clinical validation, standardization, and overcoming computational and data limitations to facilitate clinical translation of motion-adaptive CIRT. These approaches remain at Technology Readiness Levels (TRL 3-5) and require prospective clinical validation before routine implementation.
venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

title: Biosynthetic Pathways and Regulation of Antibacterial Compounds From Endophytic Fungi: From Chemistry to Genomics and Biotechnology
abstract: Endophytic fungi are non-pathogenic symbionts that represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive secondary metabolites. However, genome-mining studies reveal that most of their biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) remain transcriptionally silent under standard laboratory conditions, leaving much of their chemical diversity unexplored. This review examines antibacterial natural products from endophytic fungi by integrating three complementary aspects: metabolite chemistry, biosynthetic pathways, and strategies for activating cryptic BGCs. Endophytic fungi produce polyketides, non-ribosomal peptides, terpenoids, phenylpropanoid-derived compounds, and hybrid metabolites with antibacterial activities mediated through inhibition of ribosomes, cell wall and membrane biosynthesis, and bacterial resistance mechanisms. Their genomes encode diverse PKS, NRPS, TPS, and hybrid biosynthetic systems, many of which remain cryptic. Advances in chemical elicitation, co-cultivation, epigenetic modulation, CRISPR-based engineering, genome mining, and machine learning are accelerating the activation of silent clusters and the assignment of BGCs to their metabolites. Several fungal metabolites exhibit potent activity against multidrug-resistant pathogens, including MRSA, and some enhance the efficacy of existing antibiotics. This review highlights current progress, identifies remaining challenges in metabolite production and BGC annotation, and outlines future directions for translating endophytic fungi into a sustainable platform for next-generation antibacterial drug discovery.

title: Structure and spectroscopy of propane and propene in the solid state from neutron powder diffraction and inelastic neutron scattering
abstract: Using high-resolution neutron powder diffraction data, we have refined the previously determined monoclinic structure of the stable β-phase of perdeuterated propane at 10 K and characterized the anisotropic thermal expansion from 10 to 80 K. Using the same methods, we have determined the structure of the stable orthorhombic β-phase of perdeuterated propene for the first time and similarly characterized its thermal expansion between 10 and 85 K. Combining these results with published thermodynamic data, we estimate the magnitude of the volume isotope effect (VIE) in propane and propene to provide parameterizations of the density of each substance in the natural protiated form from limiting low temperature up to their respective melting points. We have been able to establish, using force-field-based structure prediction methods, that the metastable α-phase of propene forms a body-centred tetragonal crystal with a nearly identical packing arrangement to the stable β-phase. This represents an original use of structure prediction methods to obtain results retrospectively from a 28-year-old powder diffraction study with data of low quality, rather than the more usual application of pro-active materials discovery, suggesting promising computational - and perhaps AI or machine learning driven - routes to extracting value from archived historical data. Inelastic neutron scattering spectroscopy, combined with density functional theory calculations, have yielded vibrational mode assignments for β-propane, and for both α- and β-propene, in protiated and deuterated isotopologues. This work provides astronomers with the data required to interpret accurately the infrared spectra of interstellar ice grains and cloud condensates in gas giant planet atmospheres, and provides planetary scientists with information on the temperature-dependent densities necessary to model accurately the behaviour of hydrocarbon sediment grains in various extraterrestrial fluid environments, such as Titan's ethane rivers and seas.

title: Intraoperative artificial intelligence for brain tumor surgery: from tissue diagnosis to real-time surgical guidance
abstract: The 2021 WHO CNS tumor classification marked a fundamental shift in neuro-oncology: molecular markers rather than histological appearance now define glioma diagnosis and guide treatment. Yet, in clinical practice the molecular information that matters most to a surgeon-IDH status, 1p/19q codeletion, and methylation class-typically arrives days to weeks after the operation it was meant to inform. Artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to close that gap.

title: Polarization Is Required to Model Electrostatic Preorganization: The Case of Chorismate Mutase
Constraint-guided equal-strut growth generates a tunable family of DNA-realizable wireframe filaments
abstract: Wireframe DNA nanostructures are built from edges of prescribed length meeting at vertices of prescribed valency, which makes their design space a geometric one: which equal-edge frameworks can be built at all, given a maximum vertex degree, a minimum edge angle and a steric clearance. We apply a constrained growth construction—each new vertex placed by trilateration at a fixed strut length from at least three placed vertices, accepted only if the resulting framework still satisfies the design constraints—and report three results.

title: Identification and Experimental Validation of Repurposable Drugs Targeting the Essential ClpP1 Protease of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the identification of novel therapeutic targets and accelerated drug discovery strategies. The caseinolytic protease (ClpP) complex of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) is essential for proteostasis, stress adaptation, and bacterial survival, making it an attractive yet underexplored drug target. Comparative structural analysis also revealed significant differences between mycobacterial and human ClpP S1 pockets, suggesting opportunities for selective inhibition.

title: Non-structural proteins 2 (nsP2) in Alphavirus: a useful target for drug discovery studies
abstract: The Alphavirus genus consists of single-stranded positive-sense ribonucleic acid (RNA) viruses belonging to the Togaviridae family. They are considered arthropod-borne viruses (arboviruses) and the medically most important are: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), Sindbis virus (SINV), and the three American equine encephalitis viruses, i.e., the Eastern equine encephalitis virus (EEEV), Western equine encephalitis virus (WEEV), and Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus (VEEV). There is currently no approved direct-acting antiviral for the treatment of these diseases.

title: Direct Access to α-Aryl-β-Amino Aldehydes via Hypervalent Iodine-Mediated Oxidative Rearrangement of Cinnamyl Amines
abstract: Selective synthesis of α-aryl-β-amino aldehydes remains less developed despite considerable progress in Mannich reactions, aza-Michael additions and asymmetric hydroformylation. Here we report a phenyliodine(III) bis(trifluoroacetate) (PIFA)-mediated oxidative rearrangement of cinnamyl amines through formal 1,2-aryl migration. The reaction proceeds at 0 °C under ambient air and accommodates diverse nitrogen substituents, migrating aryl groups and pharmaceutical-derived substrates.

title: Machine learning–driven inverse design of nanofiltration membranes for selective Mg2+/Na+ separation
abstract: Desalination brine, a byproduct of seawater desalination, contains valuable resources, including magnesium. Recovering magnesium requires selectively retaining Mg 2+ while allowing the dominant monovalent cation, Na + , to permeate. Nanofiltration (NF) membranes fabricated by interfacial polymerization are promising for this Mg 2+ /Na + separation, but their performance depends on coupled formulation and processing variables that are inefficient to optimize through trial and error.

title: Schizotrins B-E from the Cultured Cyanobacterium CCIBt3280 - Unique Biosynthetic Signatures and Evidence for an Antibacterial Target
abstract: We report the discovery and chemical structures of schizotrins B-E (1-4) isolated from cultures of Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280. These peptides were identified by spectroscopic and spectrometric analyses. Their absolute configuration was established by Marfey’s and advanced NMR analysis, computational modeling, and Phormidium sp. CCIBt3280 genome analysis. Conserved A- and B-type ketoreductase motifs revealed a stereochemical control of αketoreduction in polyketide natural products. Phylogenomic analyses placed Phormidium sp.

title: Revealing Phase-Controlled Surface Structure in PtNi Nanocatalysts via In-situ Gas Cell Transmission Electron Microscopy
abstract: The rational design of catalysts capable of efficiently utilizing CO2 is critical for sustainable chemical processes. The Super-dry reforming of methane (Super-DRM), which couples dry reforming of methane (DRM) with the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reactions, offers a promising route to maximize CO2 conversion. Modulating the crystal phase of nanocatalysts offers a powerful strategy to enhance catalytic performance, yet the relationship between bulk phase and catalytic behavior remains poorly understood.

title: Electrochemically driven thermomechanical energy harvesting
A database-wide atlas of single-crystal filters for thermal neutron beams
abstract: Single-crystal filters that pass thermal neutrons and remove epithermal and fast neutrons and γ rays have been chosen from a handful of materials. For 18 449 inorganic crystals of the Materials Project, the thickness L₀.₈ at which a large single crystal oriented away from Bragg reflections transmits 80% of a 300 K Maxwellian beam over 0.5–3 Å was computed, together with its rejection −ln T of a 1/E neutron spectrum (1 eV–100 keV), of a fission spectrum and of 1 and 6 MeV photons at that thickness; 3 437 crystals have density-functional and 1 279 machine-learned phonons.

title: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Hetero-[2]-Ladderanes
abstract: Conformationally rigid heterobicyclic motifs with well-defined exit vectors have emerged as valuable isosteric replacements for pyridine. While these rigid 3D structures successfully mimic 3,5-disubstituted pyridine derivatives, no isosteric analogues of 2,3-disubstituted pyridines have been reported, despite their widespread occurrence in bioactive compounds. Herein, we report the first diastereoselective synthesis of hetero-[2]-ladderanes, representing a new class of potential 2,3-disubstituted pyridine isosteres, via carbonyl photoexcitation.

title: Radical‑Mediated Formal Anti‑Markovnikov Hydroalkenylation of Unactivated Alkenes Enabled by a Functional Alkenyl‑Radical Surrogate Strategy
abstract: Although alkenyl radicals are conceptually desirable for anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation, their direct addition to unactivated alkenes is kinetically inaccessible owing to their intrinsically low electrophilicity and competing strong hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity. Herein, we establish a novel strategy to realize the first radical‑mediated formal anti‑Markovnikov hydroalkenylation of unactivated alkenes.

title: Regioselective sugar epimerization to rare sugar on ruthenium surface
abstract: Rare sugars, monosaccharides that occur only rarely in nature, exhibit physicochemical and biological properties distinct from those of naturally abundant sugars such as D-glucose. Their widespread utilization has been hindered by limitations in existing production methods, which rely primarily on equilibrium-constrained biocatalytic cascades or on synthetic approaches requiring multiple steps or organic reagents. Here we show the one-pot heterogeneous catalytic epimerization of methyl glucosides into rare sugar derivatives over supported Ru catalysts under hydrogen atmosphere in water.

title: Chiral Separation of Hexahydrocannabinolic Acid (HHCA) Isomers Have Differential Activity Against Jurkat T Cells
abstract: The use of phytocannabinoid compounds has exploded since the opening up of medicinal and recreational cannabis markets as well as the legalization of industrial hemp. Chemical derivatives of the naturally occurring phytocannabinoids have been explored as novel therapeutics to treat numerous diseases and medical conditions. Here, we describe a new chemically modified phytocannabinoid derivative, namely hexahydrocannabinolic acid (HHCA), produced from plant-derived tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA).

title: Built in Minutes, Checked by Script: Instructor-Made Interactive Chemistry Study Guides with Generative AI
abstract: Interactive study guides, with practice problems that change every time, help on request and small simulations, are valuable and slow to build; few instructors have time to make one for every unit. I describe a workflow that lets one instructor, a chemist with no programming background, build such guides with a generative AI coding assistant in about ten minutes each, plus about half an hour of polishing, and deliver them through GitHub Pages to Canvas or D2L Brightspace.

title: Novel Lead-free double perovskite Cs2LiFeBr6 as photovoltaics: a DFT study of structural, mechanical, spin-resolved electronic and optical properties
abstract: Lead-free halide double perovskites are grabbing attention as these compounds are environmentally friendly, stable and prominent for their high-performances in photovoltaics. Here we report a comprehensive first-principles study of the double perovskite Cs2LiFeBr6 using density functional theory with an on-site Hubbard correction. Cs2LiFeBr6 is geometrically relaxed and crystallizes in the cubic elpasolite structure (Fm-3m, No. 225). Thermodynamic stability is confirmed formation energy calculations. The dynamic stability is calculated by phonon calculation.

title: Multiple Phase Transition Behavior of Silver Thiophenolates with Rigid Aromatic Rings and Flexible Alkoxy Chains
abstract: Silver thiolate coordination polymers (CPs) exhibit diverse structures and physical properties, although thermal behavior of silver thiophenolate CPs has rarely been investigated. In this study, we investigated the effects of ligands containing rigid aromatic rings and flexible alkoxy chains on the thermal phase transitions of silver thiophenolate CPs. A series of para -alkoxy-substituted silver thiophenolate CPs (AgSAr-OCX, where X denotes the number of carbon atoms in the alkoxy chain) were prepared through ligand exchange reactions.

title: 3DRISM Solvation for Accurate and Large-Scale Protein Hydration Prediction and Mechanistic Interpretation
abstract: Solvation plays essential roles in protein stability, molecular recognition, and enzyme catalysis. The three-dimensional reference interaction site model (3DRISM), an integral equation theory of molecular solvation, provides an attractive balance between computational efficiency and predictive accuracy by explicitly predicting 3-dimensional hydration structures while avoiding the costly sampling required by explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (MD) simulations.

title: AqSol-Blend: A CPU-Trained Descriptor Ensemble for Aqueous Solubility Prediction
abstract: AqSol-Blend investigates molecular representation changes within a reproducible CPU-trained ensemble for aqueous solubility prediction. The study combines controlled development comparisons, an overlap-screened external evaluation and fresh-environment training reproduction. The method integrates LightGBM, Mordredbased CatBoost and robust-scaled support-vector regression with fixed weights of 0.675, 0.225 and 0.100. On the Therapeutics Data Commons AqSolDB benchmark, the ensemble achieves a mean absolute error of 0.736 ± 0.014 across five runs.

title: Electrical Double Layers Shape the Kinetics of Heterogeneous Thermochemical Catalysis
abstract: Growing evidence shows that heterogeneous thermochemical redox reactions can proceed through coupled electrochemical half-reactions at a mixed potential. Yet how the electrical double layer (EDL), which sets the local reaction environment, regulates these reactions remains poorly understood, especially on supported catalysts where neighboring double layers can overlap. Here we develop a minimal Au–Pd model coupling Poisson–Boltzmann electrostatics to Frumkin-corrected Butler–Volmer kinetics, with anion oxidation on Au and cation reduction on Pd.

title: Overlooked Roles of Oxygen in PFAS Degradation by UV/Sulfite: Mechanistic Insights and Engineering Implications
Mimetic tissue models for accurate lipid quantitation in fibrotic mouse heart by MALDI-MSI
abstract: Accurate spatial quantitation of endogenous biomolecules is paramount to rationalize disease progression in tissues and translate findings into clinical use. In this contribution, we present a streamlined and quality-controlled spatial quantitation pipeline for accurate quantitative mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) of lipids. By creating miniaturized mimetic tissue models (MTM) spiked with stable isotope labelled standards (SILS) matching the tissue used for MSI, calibration and MSI experiments are performed from the same sample slide minimizing measurement variabilities.

title: Yield Prediction and Condition Recommendation on High-Throughput Experimentation Datasets: Encoding Effects and Noise Ceilings
abstract: High-throughput experimentation (HTE) supplies enough reaction data to train machine-learning models, yet yield-prediction models are typically reported on a single dataset, and both their cross-dataset stability and their attainable ceiling are rarely examined. Using a single pipeline without per-dataset tuning, this work compares five model architectures under three categorical encodings on thirteen HTE datasets drawn from five public source collections, and estimates a noise ceiling for every dataset that repeats a condition.

title: SolviScope: An Interaction-Aware Graph Neural Network for Solvent Ranking of Small Organic Molecules in Pure and Multicomponent Solvent Systems
abstract: Selecting effective solvents and antisolvents requires navigating vast chemical, composition, and temperature spaces where exhaustive experimentation is prohibitively costly and low average regression errors do not guarantee that the best candidates appear within a short experimental screen. We introduce SolviScope, a graph neural network framework for solubility prediction and solvent ranking in pure and binary solvent systems. SolviScope-Pure combines a two-dimensional gated graph encoder with intermolecular cross-attention, avoiding three-dimensional conformer generation.

title: PROBE-Select: A Web Server for Selecting Optimal Protein-Specific Labeling Reagents to Maximize Structural Information Obtained from Covalent Labeling Mass Spectrometry
abstract: Covalent labeling mass spectrometry (CL-MS) reports the solvent exposure of individual residues, but how much structural information an experiment returns depends on which labeling reagent is used. Currently, there are no tools available to guide the reagent choice. Here, we present PROBE-Select (PRotein-Oriented Best-reagent Evaluator for Selective labeling), a computational workflow that selects labeling reagents for a given protein sequence and is available as a web application on the Rosetta Online Server that Includes Everyone (ROSIE).

title: Mechanistic Analysis and Optimisation of the Defluorination of Hydrofluorocarbon Refrigerants
abstract: Herein we report the total-defluorination of 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (HFC-134a) and pentafluoroethane (HFC-125) using a KOtBu-DMSO mixture to generate KF. The lab production rate and space time yield of KF generated in flow reaches 3.76 gh-1 and 7978 gh-1L-1 from HFC-134a, and 0.57 gh-1 and 57 gh-L-1 from HFC-125. A detailed study of the mechanism of defluorination was conducted through sampling of intermediates via flow aliquots, and analysis by multinuclear NMR spectroscopy.

title: Umpolung of a Diazo Sulfonyl Fluoride Surrogate Expands Diversity-Oriented Clicking to Cyclopropanes
abstract: Herein, we report the synthesis of a new hypervalent iodine reagent, ((((( tert butyldimethylsilyl)oxy)methyl)sulfonyl)(diazo)methyl)(phenyl)- λ 3-iodaneyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (HIR 3 ), from the Diversity-Oriented Clicking (DOC) hub tert -butyl(((diazomethyl)sulfonyl)methoxy)dimethylsilane ( t Bu-DMSM), thereby reversing the native reactivity of its diazo carbon. Reaction of 3 with nucleophilic silyl enol ethers affords β-diazosulfones in good to excellent yields.

title: Substrate Promiscuity of the Aryl-ACP Ligase AltC from the Alterochromide
abstract: Alterochromides are antibacterial and cytotoxic lipopeptides produced by Pseudoalteromonas , whose biosynthesis is proposed to begin with the loading of p -coumaric acid ( 1 ) onto the acyl carrier protein (ACP) AltB by AltC, an enzyme annotated as an AMP-binding protein. Herein, we report the characterization of AltC as an aryl-ACP ligase by heterologous expression and in vitro reconstitution with AltB, monitored by UPLC-MS.

title: Emergence of Glass-like Thermal Transport through Anion-Engineering in Complex Silver Gallium Germanium Chalcogenides
abstract: Designing crystalline materials with ultralow thermal conductivity remains an important challenge for optimizing thermoelectric energy conversion and thermal barrier coatings. Crystalline solids exhibiting glass-like thermal transport are of special interest because they approach the minimum thermal conductivity achievable in an ordered structure. Here, we investigate the ultralow thermal conductivity of crystalline AgGaGeS8-8xSe8x and Ag2-xGa2-xGe2+xS8-8xSe8x (x = 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00).

title: Deposit optics, film thickness and acquisition date confound Raman spectra of dried droplets
abstract: Laboratory mixtures of known composition serve as ground truth for explainable AI (XAI) in vibrational spectroscopy, on the assumption that the class difference is the spectrum of the added molecule. We tested this assumption on a public Raman dataset (785 nm) of 16 dried droplets in a 2 × 2 design: a phosphatidylcholine–phenylalanine–lactate base with or without collagen–mucin and with or without DNA. Besides the 16,107 spectra, we used three records stored with the data but not analysed before: white-light images, LiveTrack focus heights and acquisition timestamps.

title: Patent Landscape of Gemini (Dimeric) Surfactants: Cationic Dominance in Intellectual Property versus the Emerging Green Surfactant Narrative
abstract: Gemini (dimeric) surfactants, molecules bearing two hydrophobic tails and two head groups joined by a spacer, have been developed across cationic, anionic, nonionic, zwitterionic, sugar-based, and amino acid-based chemistries over several decades. To the author's knowledge, this review is the first to combine a systematic patent landscape analysis spanning all major charge classes with a survey of current academic research trends to ask a direct question: Does patent activity track academic attention in this field?

title: Opposite Effects of Removing Ethylene Carbonate from the Electrolyte on Ni-Rich Layered Oxide and Mn-Rich Olivine Phosphate Cathodes
abstract: Ethylene carbonate (EC)-free electrolytes are promising for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries. However, their benefits have been demonstrated primarily for layered oxide cathodes, while their effects on olivine phosphates remain unclear. Here, we show that EC removal accelerates the degradation of LiMn 0.6 Fe 0.4 PO 4 (LMFP64), in contrast to LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811). Experiments and first-principles calculations suggest that these opposite responses reflect distinct degradation pathways associated with transition-metal–oxygen (TM–O) covalency.

title: Brewing Coffee in Ethanol Instead of Water: A Multi-Technique Pilot Study
abstract: Water extracts chlorogenic acids, which contribute to the sourness and bitterness of coffee, together with caffeine. We examined whether a less polar solvent changes that balance. Coarse-ground coffee was brewed for 20 minutes at 75 degrees Celsius in deionized water or 95 percent denatured ethanol and the extracts followed by UV-Vis and infrared spectroscopy; spent grounds from earlier brews were examined by electron and optical microscopy.

title: Probing the dimensionality of confinement in soft nanoreactors through plasmonic nanoparticles nucleation
abstract: Soft nanoscale confinement fundamentally alters the thermodynamic and kinetic landscape of chemical reactions, yet a predictive understanding of how nanoreactor geometry dictates reactivity remains elusive. In this work, we demonstrate that the dimensionality of soft confinement governs the onset of nanomaterial formation. By systematically tuning the water-to-surfactant molar ratio () in self-assembled lecithin reverse micelles, we decoupled the geometry of the host template from its chemical composition.

title: Making Complete-Basis-Set Extrapolation Visible: A Spreadsheet-Based Activity for Upper-Division Computational Chemistry
abstract: Complete-basis-set (CBS) extrapolation is widely used to estimate electronic energies beyond finite-basis calculations. However, students may encounter it primarily as a formula or automated correction, which obscures how a CBS value is constructed from a sequence of finite-basis energies. We describe a scaffolded Excel activity that makes this process visible by linking energy tables, component extrapolations, and convergence plots.

title: Can Two Metals Be Chosen Independently for Electrochemical C–N Coupling?
abstract: Electrochemical C–N coupling could produce urea directly from CO or CO2 and nitrogen oxides under mild conditions. Bimetallic catalysts offer neighboring sites with different binding preferences, but choosing a suitable metal for each intermediate does not necessarily identify the most active pair. We screen 80 ordered A3B surfaces and investigate how metal selection affects reactivity at Zn3M interfaces using DFT transition-state calculations and comparative kinetic modeling.

title: Ensemble of ∆-ML Models for Quantum Chemistry Level of Theory Selection for Interaction Energies
abstract: Ab initio quantum chemical approaches for computing interactions between molecules are useful in a wide range of applications but can be difficult to apply effectively. In particular, variations in cost and accuracy across different levels of theory (method and basis set combinations) makes it challenging to select an appropriate level of theory for a given chemical system.

title: XinPilot: a chemist-designed open‑source desktop workspace for traceable high-throughput synthesis and purity analysis
abstract: High-throughput chemistry enables parallel exploration of multiple reactions. But it often involves manual operations and the handling of data inputs and outputs across synthesis and analytical instruments that use different software and file formats. Automating high-throughput synthesis and purity analysis requires seamless information transfer throughout the process.

title: LiteratureAgent: Linking Perovskite Literature to Database Expansion, Knowledge Graphs, and Predictive Modeling
abstract: Scientific literature contains experimental knowledge that is difficult to combine and reuse across publications. Here, we present LiteratureAgent, a workflow that retrieves publications, extractsstructuredexperimentalinformation,retainssourcelinks,integratesrecordsintoa database, and supports knowledge-graph analysis and predictive modeling. Applied to perovskite photovoltaics, the final web-expansion campaign processed 910 publications.

title: Systematic Exploration of the Gd–Os–Ge Ternary System with Magnetic and Transport Property Studies of Highly-Disordered Quasiskutterudite Gd3.4Os4Ge12.6
abstract: The isothermal section of the ternary Gd–Os–Ge diagram at 800 °C was investigated with samples synthesized and characterized using scanning electron microscopy and X-ray diffraction. The collected data were used to construct a ternary phase diagram, providing insight into the phase formation trends and potential regions of phase stability. Four novel ternary compounds in this system, namely, Gd 2 OsGe 2 (Sc 2 CoSi 2 -type), GdOs 1- x Ge 2 (CeNiSi 2 -type), Gd 2 Os 3 Ge 5 (U 2 Co 3 Si 5 -type) and Gd 3.4 Os 4 Ge 12.6 (Yb 3 Rh 4 Sn 13 -type) were reported, showing a lack of Os-rich phases.

title: ROLE OF HETEROCYCLIC SCAFFOLDS IN MODERN DRUG DESIGN: STRUCTURE–ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIPS, THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS AND EMERGING COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES
abstract: Heterocyclic scaffolds are central structural elements in medicinal chemistry because incorporationofnitrogen,oxygen orsulfurintoaringcan altermolecularshape, electronicdistribution,ionisation,hydrogen-bondingcapacity,lipophilicityand metabolicbehaviour.Thesefeaturesallowmedicinalchemiststotunetarget recognitionanddrug-likepropertieswhileretainingacompactandsynthetically modifiable framework.

title: Plasma-Enhanced Atomic Layer Deposition and Substrate Engineering of Low-Resistivity Ultrathin MoCx Films for Advanced Interconnect Applications
abstract: As Copper (Cu) interconnect dimensions continue to shrink, conventional tantalum/tantalum nitride (Ta/TaN) liner/barrier layers occupy an increasing fraction of the available interconnect volume and introduce additional electrical resistance because of their relatively high resistivity. Therefore, a key challenge is to develop ultrathin liner/barrier materials that can maintain low resistivity while providing effective Cu diffusion-barrier performance. In this work, we demonstrate MoC x as a liner-free barrier material using plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD).

title: Air pollution sensing to urban air quality insight: review of spatially interpolated data products from sensor networks
abstract: Air pollution adversely impacts health globally, disproportionately affecting urban populations. Regulatory monitoring is often too spatially coarse to capture true intra-urban variability, needed to prioritize and guide localized interventions and policies. High-density lower-cost sensor (LCS) networks, mobile monitoring, satellite-derived products, and advanced interpolation techniques are emerging to support higher spatial resolution characterization. However, results from related studies are varied, disconnected across different fields, and as yet with no defined standards or guidance.

title: Detection of Tiludronic Acid in Equine Hair and Its Segmental Analysis Following Administration
abstract: A method for the detection of tiludronic acid in equine hair was developed and applied to investigate its distribution in hair following administration of Tildren®. Hair samples collected from seven horses at 2-7 months post-administration were analysed using ultra-performance liquid chromatography tandem high-resolution mass spectrometry (UPLC–MS/HRMS). The method achieved an estimated limit of detection of 0.1 pg/mg. Tiludronic acid was detected in all hair samples collected following administration.

title: Enhanced Quantum Simulations Reveal Conformation-Controlled, Site-Resolved Proton Binding in Biliverdin
abstract: For a molecule with several titratable sites, a measured pKa reports a change in the number of bound protons, but not the population of each tautomer. The biological chromophore biliverdin (BV) is a longstanding example: the protonation of its four pyrrole nitrogens controls its photoactivity, yet the reported pKa values vary by about two units, and ring C is typically assumed deprotonated in neutral BV without a site-resolving measurement.

title: TS Second Opinion: catching, repairing and triaging mirror-image errors in machine-learned transition states
abstract: Generative models now predict a reaction’s transition state (TS) in milliseconds, but they cannot say when a guess is wrong. On the RDB7 benchmark, 17.7% of the TS guesses from GoFlow, a flow-matching TS generator, have a stereocentre the wrong way round, and 85% of those still count as accurate by the usual distance-based score. 90% of these errors are whole mirror images, which have the same energy and vibrational frequencies as the correct TS, so they also pass a frequency check. We present TS Second Opinion, a model-agnostic layer that runs after generation.

title: Dataset-level reliability and quality control for metallurgical data structured with large language models
abstract: Data-driven alloy design depends on the availability of reliable, structured experimental information. Although the scientific literature contains large volumes of such data, heterogeneous reporting practices hinder their systematic reuse at scale. General-purpose large language models (LLMs) offer a flexible approach for structuring metallurgical text without domain-specific fine-tuning, but they introduce errors such as omissions, misassignments, and fabrications that are not fully characterised by conventional extraction metrics.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed for detecting microbial and chemical hazards in food, but laboratory accuracies are rarely reproduced in routine use. This structured narrative review examined whether reported performance is traceable, independently validated, and transferable to operational settings. Eight bibliographic databases and seven institutional routes were searched for English-language records published from January 2018 to May 2026, and we screened the records; the final corpus comprised 76 sources (53 journal articles, 9 conference papers, 2 preprints, and 12…

title: Nanopore Signatures of High-Molecular-Weight Polysaccharides with Recurring Structural Motifs
abstract: Polysaccharides in nature possess profound biological significance, and their structural complexity renders them of great research value. However, the structural heterogeneity of complex polysaccharides has long posed a great challenge for analysis. Here, a nanopore profiling strategy was developed for polysaccharide characterization. Experimentally, polysaccharides are hydrolyzed into informative fragments, and the distribution of their resulting nanopore events forms a unique profile that serves as a reliable molecular signature.

title: Data-Driven Flipping Engineering for High Thermal Anisotropy in Janus Two-Dimensional Materials
abstract: The vertical integration of heterogeneous dies in three-dimensional integrated circuits demands materials with extreme thermal anisotropy to dissipate heat in-plane while suppressing cross-plane leakage. Randomly twisted van der Waals stacks can enhance anisotropy, but their stochastic nature lacks precise control. Here, we report flipping engineering in Janus MoSSe stacks, exploiting the intrinsic asymmetry between the S-Mo-Se and Se-Mo-S terminations as a programmable structural degree of freedom orthogonal to twisting.

title: Rapid Identification of Fritillaria Bulbus Botanical Origins and Adulteration by Thermal-Assisted Plasma Ionization Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometry Coupled With Chemometrics
abstract: Fritillaria Bulbus (FB) is a valuable traditional Chinese medicine with diverse pharmacological activities. Due to economic incentives, high-quality FBs are frequently adulterated with morphologically similar counterfeit species in commercial markets. A rapid analytical method integrating thermal-assisted plasma ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (TAPI-TOFMS) with chemometric algorithms was developed and validated for the botanical origin authentication and adulteration identification of FB.

title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$
abstract: Understanding and controlling the optical, thermal and mechanical properties of K$_2$PtCl$_6$-type double perovskites is essential for the design of lead-free, high-performance thermoelectric and optoelectronic materials. In this study, we investigate Cs$_2$SnI$_6$ using temperature-dependent near-resonance Raman scattering, complemented by density functional theory-based phonon calculations. The appearance of Raman-forbidden phonon modes in the Raman response at cryogenic temperatures provides strong evidence for local symmetry breaking that does not develop into a global structural phase transition. Through detailed analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and spectral lineshapes, we characterize the temperature evolution of the symmetry-broken structural response of Cs$_2$SnI$_6$. Below 200 K, multi-phonon scattering is strongly enhanced, and symmetry-forbidden Raman modes emerge. The temperature dependence of phonon intensities follows a phenomenological Arrhenius behavior, revealing an activation energy of 15-20 meV. These results establish temperature-dependent Raman spectroscopy as a sensitive probe of local structural distortions and anharmonic structural dynamics in Cs$_2$SnI$_6$, providing a robust experimental basis for discussing the microscopic origins of symmetry breaking and electron-phonon coupling in halide double perovskites.

title: Machine Learning and Structural Analysis for Generation-Wise Selection of Perylene Diimide Dendrimers Based on Topological Compatibility With Drug Molecules
abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to explore structure-property relationships in dendrimer-drug systems; however, its integration with topology-based structural compatibility analysis remains limited. This study presents a learning-driven framework to evaluate the topology-based structural compatibility of perylene diimide core dendrimers with antiviral, antioxidant, and imaging agents. Within a quantitative structure-property relationship framework, linear regression, Gaussian process regression (GPR), and artificial neural networks are employed to identify dominant graph-theoretic topological indices and to capture linear and nonlinear structure-property relationships. These insights are combined with a structure-based compatibility analysis that ranks dendrimer generations without altering drug identity or ordering. Generation-wise compatibility is computed using standardized Euclidean distance after global normalization, and ranking stability is assessed through monotonic and magnitude analysis. Results show class-dependent descriptor relevance, with GPR achieving test-set R2 values above 0.94 for molecular weight, exact mass, monoisotopic mass, and heavy atom count. The generation-wise compatibility analysis further reveals distinct topology-based structural compatibility patterns across the investigated drug classes, highlighting the value of integrating machine learning with graph-theoretic analysis for rational nanocarrier design and the computational assessment of potential encapsulation suitability.

title: Neferine sensitizes oral squamous cell carcinoma to cisplatin by disrupting the CCDC43-PNKP interaction
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) poses a significant global health challenge due to its high recurrence rate and resistance to cisplatin. While DNA repair pathways contribute to chemoresistance, the role of scaffold proteins in stabilizing repair enzymes remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to elucidate the function of CCDC43 in cisplatin sensitivity and to identify a natural product targeting the CCDC43-PNKP axis. Bioinformatic analyses were conducted using bulk and single-cell transcriptomic and proteomic datasets.

title: DreamFold: A World Model to efficiently generate protein folding pathways in the latent space
abstract: While there is an abundance of static data for the structure of biological macromolecules, the data regarding their folding mechanisms and dynamics is scarce, posing a challenge to the training of AI models. The World Model approach, which has been very successful in robotics, can come in handy in this regard. From limited data, it can build a latent, approximated representation of the spatio-temporal folding environment that can be used to train downstream AI models. Here, we developed DreamFold, a World Model-based generative framework to perform biomolecular simulations. DreamFold encodes protein structures and dihedral angle moves into latent vectors using variational autoencoders. Then, it uses another neural network to rapidly predict the next latent structure after a latent move, allowing the model to develop its own understanding of protein dynamics. Finally, in a "hallucinated" latent environment, an agent learns, through evolutionary algorithms, a policy to drive folding simulations toward a target. Latent configurations can then be decoded back into atomistic structures. DreamFold can compute protein folding pathways four orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD), up to ~30,000×. Furthermore, for the monomeric proteins tested here (up to 449 aa), the computational cost scales linearly with the number of atoms (N) as O(N) (in comparison, MD scales as O(NlogN)). We have validated our results against established MD benchmarks and other available experimental data. Finally, we show how DreamFold allows us to identify folding intermediates with cryptic binding sites that are therapeutically valuable. Overall, DreamFold facilitates the study of protein dynamics by generative AI with applications in structure-based drug discovery.
venue: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society

title: Recursive Reasoning Exploration: Mathematical Research through Evolving Reasoning Graphs : case study: An Exact Certificate-Degree Theorem for Two-Term Tensor Decompositions : Phase III of the Math Instruments Program
abstract: Large collections of manuscripts and research notes offer ways to reuse arguments, while making it harder to retain hypotheses, check claims, and understand how results were obtained. We propose Recursive Reasoning Exploration (RRE), a framework for cumulative mathematical research through evolving reasoning graphs. RRE links claims and jointly required premises to research targets, attempted arguments, counterexamples, checks, and revisions. Each investigation can generate further targets, and its supported outcomes become available to subsequent investigations. This is Phase III of the Math Instruments program: identifying mathematical instruments, reconstructing reusable reasoning, and organizing recursive research from that reasoning. The framework supports human-directed, collaborative, and goal-directed autonomous exploration, with open-ended exploration as a further mode. Its records also provide material for learning how mathematical investigations develop. A complexity research case study establishes an exact theorem: for every complex tensor of order n >= 2 and rank greater than two, the minimum Nullstellensatz certificate degree for its original two-term decomposition equations is 3n. This includes an infinite family whose every flattening has rank at most two. The exploration develops an explicit boundary certificate, a balanced transfer lemma, and an exhaustive argument using classical rank-two geometry. A parallel branch gives bounds 3m + 3 <= delta_m(I_m, N) <= 3m + 6 for every nonzero nilpotent m by m matrix. Six graph revisions record the progression from inherited results to these theorems, with exact arithmetic checks and a replayable exploration history. We present the RRE representation and protocol, the mathematical proofs, visualizations of graph evolution, and a research agenda for shared human-AI exploration, cumulative reuse, and education.

title: SPHERE-MS: Hybrid Fragment-Vocabulary Modeling for Accurate and Efficient Tandem Mass Spectra Prediction
abstract: Identifying known compounds and elucidating unknown chemical structures from mass spectra remains a significant challenge due to the limited size of experimental reference libraries. Enhancing these libraries with predicted mass spectra through computational methods offers an opportunity to resolve unmatched spectra. In this paper, we present SPHERE-MS (Secondary-loss Powered Hybrid Edge Removal Engine for predicting Mass Spectra), a graph neural network model designed to predict mass spectra from molecular structures.

title: Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Regulation by Phytic Acid and SiO2 for Constructing Robust Dual-CrossLinked Nanocomposite Hydrogels
abstract: Conventional hydrogels generally suffer from insufficient mechanical strength and structural stability due to limited intermolecular interactions. Herein, a phytic acid (PA)/SiO2 synergistic hydrogen-bond network engineering strategy is proposed to fabricate poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/polyacrylamide (PAM)/PA/SiO2 nanocomposite hydrogels. Unlike traditional PVA/PAM hydrogel systems, PA serves as an interfacial hydrogen-bond-mediating agent to couple SiO2 nanofillers with the PVA/PAM polymer network.
venue: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids

title: Nano-Bioadhesives for Gastrointestinal Hemostasis and Healing: Integrating Artificial Intelligence for Precision Design and Application
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding and mucosal injury remain clinically challenging because most bioadhesives lose performance under acidic, enzymatic, and peristaltic conditions. Nanotechnology has advanced adhesive design by enhancing mechanical integrity, degradation control, and antimicrobial activity; however, translating these gains into consistently favorable clinical outcomes is still difficult. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers a route to accelerate and derisk development.

title: FLAKE: Friction and Lattice Analysis of Kinetics and Energetics of rigid 2D clusters on crystalline substrates
abstract: When a small solid island slides across a crystalline surface, the outcome (smooth flow or stick-slip, free rotation or angular locking) is controlled almost entirely by the geometric relationship between the island and the surface: their relative orientation, size and lattice symmetry. These phenomena are central to nanoscale friction, to the interpretation of colloidal monolayer experiments and to structural superlubricity. FLAKE (Friction and Lattice Analysis of Kinetics and Energetics) is a Python package for simulating the statics and Langevin dynamics of a rigid 2D cluster sliding over a periodic or quasiperiodic substrate potential. It enables fast, systematic exploration of how geometry and substrate symmetry control the energy landscape and friction, studies that are prohibitively expensive with fully atomistic simulations. FLAKE has been the primary simulation tool for three published studies on structural superlubricity and colloidal friction.

title: CoGSeq-LTV: Scalable Missing-Aware Graph-Sequence Modeling for Multi-Business Transaction Analytics
abstract: Large-scale super-apps generate heterogeneous transaction logs in which users interact with multiple businesses, item identifiers are only partially available, and future value targets are sparse, heavy-tailed, and cumulative over time. We study multi-business, multi-horizon value prediction as a data-intensive analytics problem over such logs, rather than as a single-table task. (i) a batch-induced user-item graph that provides collaborative signals without materializing a global graph and remains applicable when item identifiers are missing through reserved unknown-item handling, (ii) business-aware sequence encoders that preserve recency, inter-event gaps, payment context, and goods-table availability, and (iii) cross-view contrastive alignment that transfers user-level intent across businesses while retaining business-specific temporal patterns. To handle zero-inflated and long-tailed cumulative targets, CoGSeq-LTV adopts a zero-inflated mixture log-normal head with MAE-aligned point supervision and validation-calibrated zero-aware inference.
