Experiments on the BiBiSheng transaction-log dataset show that CoGSeq-LTV improves over representative LTV baselines across businesses and horizons, including under a later out-of-time evaluation window.

title: NEIGHBOR: Aligning Service Behaviour and Evidence Use in an LLM Agent for Community Resident Services
abstract: Residents who contact a community service desk about a repair or a service charge need answers they can act on, with facts that hold for their case and commitments the desk can keep. In tool-augmented LLM agents, such facts come from documents and records, and the conduct of a service answer is usually specified in a system prompt. We present NEIGHBOR, an LLM agent for community resident services that trains this conduct into the model that drives its tools. NEIGHBOR is deployed on a live resident-service platform for a district of an East Asian city of more than ten million people. It adapts Qwen3-235B-A22B with LoRA on 7,824 supervised fine-tuning examples built from public community-service materials around six service-behaviour targets, among them commitment control and human referral, and the adapted model plans document retrieval and read-only text-to-SQL over the resident's own records. In an offline evaluation with seven configurations, an independent domain expert rated all 350 answers to 50 stratified held-out queries. NEIGHBOR scores 7.74/10 against 5.86 for the same agent running the un-tuned model (+1.88; paired Wilcoxon $p<10^{-8}$; higher on 46 of 50 queries) and improves all six rated dimensions. No tool-augmented answer received a red-line flag (standalone models: 8-14% of answers). An LLM judge ranks the seven configurations much as the expert does (Spearman $ρ=0.93$). Its rubric counts specifics absent from the reference answer as fabricated, so it scores tool-grounded answers 1-2 points lower, enough to change which configuration ranks first. For resident-facing agents, service behaviour is a practical fine-tuning target that raises expert-rated answer quality with the tools held fixed.

title: XAS3DLive: an interactive X-ray absorption spectroscopy simulation/fitting platform for atomic 3D structure characterization
abstract: We present XAS3DLive, an integrated platform for X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) analysis that unifies machine-learning-driven XAS simulation, 3D structure visualization and editing, and experimental XAS fitting into a single interactive environment. The platform enables 3D structure visualization and manipulation, spectral analysis, and structure fitting to be performed by a web browser. Specifically, the machine-learning-based model enables rapid XAS simulation of spectral changes in response to structural variations; the 3D structure visualization and editing supports intuitive, atomic-level manipulation and precise adjustments; the global optimization algorithm helps to achieve automatically a detailed 3D structure of a material in an experimental XAS fitting. Multiple toolkits are provided to facilitate XAS data analysis, such as multi-spectrum comparison, energy shift, difference spectrum analysis, and quantitative evaluation. With the machine-learning model trained for inorganic complex systems with 3d transition metals, XAS3DLive is now available for K-edge XANES simulation of all ten 3d transition metals, providing a focused capability for a wide range of commonly studied transition-metal-based materials. XAS3DLive has been used for the structure analysis of Mn-doped Co3O4 and the Jahn-Teller effect has been successfully confirmed in experimental XAS fitting. This platform significantly lowers the barrier to entry for XAS analysis, improves the efficiency of XAS simulation and experimental XAS fitting, and enhances an understanding of the structure-XAS relationship through intuitive interaction.

title: Parameterisation of NMC and LFP 4680 cells for electrochemical and thermal modelling
abstract: An electrochemical-thermal model of the 4680 cylindrical cell is presented: a Doyle-Fuller-Newman model of the electrode stack coupled to a two-node thermal balance of the roll and the can (a thermal DFN, TDFN), solved by an implicit finite-volume scheme. Two cells are parameterised from teardown geometry and open literature, with every value tagged by provenance: the Tesla NMC811/graphite tabless cell and the BYD FC4680 LiFePO4 multi-tab cell. The reaction heat is evaluated at the open-circuit potential of the particle-mean concentration, which restores the heat of mixing. Both sets are calibrated in the same way, with the test fixture identified from the measurement alone. Against the 1C and 2C charge test of Ank et al., the calibrated NMC set follows the mean can temperature within 0.52 and 1.46 K, with a contact heat of 0.94 mOhm matching the authors' estimate for their holder. For the LFP cell, 1C and 2C discharges to 2.0 V were measured on the authors' bench; the fixture conductance (0.337 W/K) follows from the energy balance and the heat capacity (277 J/K) from the cooling. With the end-of-lithiation drop of LiFePO4 restored in the cathode open-circuit potential, the calibrated set follows the can temperature within 0.44 K (1C) and 0.76 K (2C), reproduces the peaks and the relaxation after cut-off. What remains is what a single can node and a single representative particle do not describe: the axial gradient of the NMC can under contact heating, and a gradual decline of the LFP voltage before the knee at 2C, which points to the distribution of particle states in the electrode. The parameter sets (BPX, CSV) and the bench data are openly available.

title: Pore-scale mechanisms of capillary imbibition in cement-based materials revealed by direct numerical simulations in a realistic FIB-SEM microstructure
abstract: Moisture transport in cement-based materials involves transient multiphase flow through highly irregular pore networks, where evolving air--water interfaces strongly influence liquid invasion and gas displacement. Here, pore-resolved, image-based direct numerical simulations (DNS) are used to investigate spontaneous imbibition in a FIB--SEM-reconstructed cementitious microstructure, resolving air--water interface dynamics at nanometre-to-micrometre spatial scales and nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales. As these dynamics remain inaccessible to direct experimental observation at such scales, the simulations provide, to the best of our knowledge, the first direct view of transient imbibition within the capillary porosity of a realistic cementitious microstructure. The three-dimensional simulations reveal highly heterogeneous wetting-front propagation, continuous interface reconfiguration, and progressive air entrapment, showing that local dynamics depend on evolving interface curvature and capillary-pressure fields rather than on characteristic pore size alone. Significant air entrapment develops even within the capillary pores and under perfectly water-wetting conditions, progressively reducing the saturation rate, while the capillary pressure of trapped-air clusters depends strongly on local interface geometry rather than gas volume alone. Controlled two-dimensional analyses show that the balance between capillary, viscous, inertial, and gravitational effects is strongly scale-dependent. Comparison with the three-dimensional simulations highlights the importance of out-of-plane interface curvature and pore-network connectivity. The framework also resolves moisture conditions at the steel--concrete interface, illustrating its potential for corrosion-relevant pore-scale analysis.

title: Symmetry-Based Transport Criterion and Robust Design for RuO$_2$-type Altermagnets
abstract: Altermagnetism combines vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent spin splitting, enabling spin-transport functionalities without ferromagnetism. Although rutile RuO$_2$ has been proposed as a d-wave altermagnet, its magnetic ground state remains highly controversial. Moreover, existing transport verifications suffer from severe ambiguity due to the entanglement of spin-splitting effects and time-reversal-even spin-Hall contributions. Here, we introduce a two-pronged strategy to break the current verification impasse. First, we establish a definitive, symmetry-based transport criterion: by identifying specific crystallographic geometries where the spin-Hall background is strictly forbidden, we provide a zero-background window for unambiguous altermagnetic detection. Concurrently, to bypass the uncertain bulk energetics, we propose the RuO$_2$/MnO$_2$ superlattice as a prototypical platform to robustly enforce the d-wave altermagnetic order via interfacial magnetic proximity. Within this platform, symmetry-resolved spin-transport analysis reveals unconventional responses, including collinear spin currents enabling field-free magnetization switching and sizable spin-polarized charge currents. By combining a universal transport criterion with a robustly engineered material platform, our work transcends the debates over bulk properties, providing an actionable, definitive experimental roadmap for verifying d-wave altermagnetism.

title: ReWY: Faster Gradient Computation for Delta-Rule Attention Family
abstract: Delta-rule linear attention underlies language models such as Kimi Linear and Qwen3-Next. Chunkwise implementations expose matrix parallelism, but their backward passes compute unnecessary auxiliary adjoints. We present ReWY, an algebraic reformulation that reduces this work before optimizing accelerator execution. Differentiating the chunk correction as one triangular residual system eliminates the inverse adjoint and reduces seven local WY matrix products to three. Two complementary transformations expose further reuse: centered matrix contractions replace pairwise vector-gate processing, and scalar-gate reductions reuse key-gradient products instead of forming a key Gram matrix. These identities simplify backward computation for DeltaNet, GDN, KDA, and GDN2 while preserving the recurrence and gradients in exact arithmetic, without changing the architecture or training objective. We implement the reduced graph on GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Under matched recomputation and full-saving policies, precision-qualified six-shape comparisons with frozen FLA references yield 1.15-1.81$\times$ geometric-mean complete low-level backward speedups on NVIDIA GPUs. All four operators achieve 1.18-1.70$\times$ on H100 and H200 while retaining original FP32 working matrices. A separate public-autograd evaluation on Ascend 950DT, including gradient conversions, yields 1.09-2.89$\times$ under available matched policies. Paired ablations establish further ReWY gains after optimizing the complementary contractions. Complete-gradient checks validate the recorded operator cases; supplementary full-model backward measurements assess integration into community FLA models and a GDN2 layer port. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/flashserve/ReWY.

title: Sequence Scanning Improves Accuracy for Antibody-Antigen and Molecular Glue Ternary Complex Cofolding
abstract: Accurately modeling biomolecular interactions is crucial for understanding biological function and can accelerate drug discovery efforts. Deep-learning-based cofolding methods such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2 can successfully predict many different biomolecular complexes. However, these models show lower success rates in predicting antibody-antigen and molecular glue (MG) ternary complexes, two cases of high relevance to pharmaceutical research.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives
abstract: BackgroundBreast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.ObjectivesTo evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and…
keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Breast Cancer; Mammography; Digital Pathology; Radiomics; Perioperative; Natural Language Processing; Systematic Review

title: Integrating Machine Learning to Identify Prognostic Subtypes and the Cisplatin Resistance Gene RRM2 in Lung Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a highly invasive malignancy associated with poor prognosis. However, reliable molecular subtypes and prognostic signatures for LUAD, particularly their associations with tumor immunity and treatment response, remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify distinct molecular subtypes and establish a robust prognostic signature for LUAD, while exploring potential therapeutic targets associated with cisplatin resistance. In this study, we integrated ten clustering algorithms with 101 machine learning methods to identify two distinct molecular subtypes of LUAD and established a robust consensus machine learning-derived signature (CMLS). Patients belonging to the Cluster A subtype exhibited a more favorable prognosis and an enhanced immune response. Furthermore, a CMLS model constructed from 19 genes exhibited strong predictive power. Individuals with high CMLS scores displayed reduced CD4 + T-cell infiltration, poorer survival outcomes, and diminished responses to immunotherapy, whereas those with the low CMLS scores showed improved clinical outcomes, better immunotherapy responsiveness, and features of an immunologically "hot" tumor phenotype. Among the identified genes, ribonucleotide reductase subunit M2 (RRM2) emerged as a core regulator associated with LUAD prognosis. RRM2 was markedly upregulated in lung cancer tissues and the LUAD cell lines and was associated with the cisplatin (DDP) resistance. Suppression of RRM2 expression significantly enhanced the cisplatin sensitivity of A549/DDP cells. In summary, our findings establish a molecular classifier that stratifies LUAD patients into distinct risk categories and highlight RRM2 as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target associated with cisplatin resistance.

title: NEVPT2 multiple spawning molecular dynamics simulations for uracil
abstract: The quasidegenerate n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (QD-NEVPT2) for complete active space reference wavefunctions has been implemented in the OpenMolcas package. The implementation utilizes the efficient formulation of Kollmar et al. for the electronic energy, which is extended here to the calculation of analytic derivatives. To demonstrate its utility, the method is applied to classical and non-adiabatic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of uracil.

title: Research Progress, Key Challenges, and Future Prospects of Raman Spectroscopy Combined With Machine Learning in Food Analysis
abstract: Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) has emerged as an important technical method for food quality and safety detection owing to its advantages, such as molecular fingerprint specificity and rapidity without damage. However, complex food matrices, susceptibility of SERS signals to fluorescence, noise, scattering interference, redundant high-dimensional spectral data, and limited model generalization ability hinder the direct application of this technique to on-site industrial detection.
venue: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: Decoupling Flavor From Spoilage: A Microbial and Chemical Framework for Volatile Sulfur Compounds and Biogenic Amines in Washed-Rind and Aged Cheeses
abstract: Ripened washed-rind and long-ripened cheeses owe their prized sulfurous, savory character to intensive proteolysis and amino-acid catabolism; the same activity, when poorly controlled, also generates sensory off-flavors and toxic biogenic amines (BAs). Histamine and tyramine reach up to approximately 2000-2500 and 1000-2000 mg/kg in extreme samples, although most cheeses contain far less, so that a 30-g portion of a high-histamine cheese can exceed the 50-mg per-meal intake regarded as without adverse effect in healthy adults.
venue: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: Covalent Organic Frameworks in Smart Food Packaging: Advances, Challenges, and Future Prospects
abstract: Food preservation challenges have positioned packaging as a rapidly evolving, innovation-driven field, with smart packaging offering transformative solutions. Among advanced materials, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have attracted growing attention due to their permanent porosity, structural tunability, high surface area, and chemical stability. These features allow COFs to address critical needs in food packaging, including active barrier protection, antimicrobial action, and smart sensing of food freshness and spoilage. This review examines recent progress in applying COFs to food packaging, with particular focus on their ability to prolong shelf life and enable smart functionalities for real-time monitoring of food quality. Safety aspects, biocompatibility, recyclability, and biodegradability are also critically evaluated, as these remain key considerations for regulatory approval and industrial translation. Although current studies report minimal cytotoxicity, long-term toxicological assessments are still limited, underscoring the need for more comprehensive investigations. Looking forward, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) provide powerful tools for accelerating COF discovery and optimization. Their integration into COF design could streamline synthesis, improve scalability, and guide application-specific material development. COFs represent a promising new class of materials poised to advance the next generation of sustainable, functional, and smart food-packaging systems.
venue: Comprehensive reviews in food science and food safety

title: A Stable Terminal Mercury Hydride and Its Reactivity To Form Mercury–Metal Bonds
abstract: Organomercury hydrides are typically encountered as unstable intermediates in organic transformations. These compounds are conventionally thought to be intrinsically unstable and have eluded isolation in the condensed phase. Here, we report the synthesis, isolation, characterization, and reactivity of an unexpectedly stable arylmercury hydride using a sterically encumbering fluorenyl-hydrindacene scaffold. The arylmercury hydride readily reacts with metalloradicals and metal hydrides to form bimetallic complexes containing unsupported mercury–metal bonds.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: GmRVE8a, a circadian clock-associated gene, negatively regulates flowering and maturity in soybean
abstract: Precise regulation of flowering time and maturity is critical for achieving high and stable soybean yields, and the circadian clock plays a central role in coordinating these developmental transitions. Soybean is a typical short-day crop with a pronounced photoperiodic response; however, the molecular mechanisms linking circadian regulation to photoperiod-dependent flowering and maturity remain incompletely understood.
venue: The Plant journal : for cell and molecular biology

title: From transcriptomics to structural modelling with AlphaFold: analysis of the central response to stress in bacteria using machine learning and structural bioinformatics
abstract: In this webinar, we will present our research focused on understanding the core mechanisms (perturbome) employed by prokaryotic organisms to survive and adapt to diverse stress conditions. Our analyses are based on transcriptomic datasets from the bacterial models Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Staphylococcus aureus, in which gene expression analyses and the prioritisation of stress-response-associated genes were performed using machine learning, systems biology, functional enrichment, and orthologous analyses.

title: Plasma untargeted metabolomics reveals distinct metabolic disturbances between sexes following inhalation of ultrafine particles and exposure to aircraft noise in mice
abstract: Traffic noise and air pollution, particularly ultrafine particles (UFP), are significantly associated with health risks. However, the systemic metabolic consequences of the combined effects of UFP and aircraft noise (AN) exposure on health remain poorly understood. We aimed to investigate changes in plasma metabolites in healthy wildtype C57BL/6J mice following whole-body inhalation exposure to UFP (average diameter <40 nm), AN and their combination (UFP+AN). Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted plasma metabolomics analysis was undertaken for UFP, AN, and combined UFP+AN-exposed mice of both sexes. This study identified a total of 1146 plasma metabolites. Across exposure groups, AN induced the greatest plasma metabolomic changes in both sexes, while UFP significantly altered metabolites only in females, indicating a sex-specific response. The combined UFP+AN exposure produced a modestly enhanced effect in males compared with either single exposure but showed an attenuated effect in females. Pathway analyses revealed that lipid and amino acid metabolism were the most affected, followed by xenobiotics, and cofactors and vitamins, after exposure in both female and male mice. Additionally, in the clean air control group, we identified sex differences in 49 plasma metabolites, which mostly included lipids and amino acids. Following exposure, however, sex-dependent metabolic differences became more pronounced and exposure-specific, suggesting that UFP and AN have distinct effects on plasma metabolome of male and female mice that extend beyond baseline sexual dimorphism observed in unexposed animals. To our knowledge, this study is the first comprehensive characterization of systemic metabolic changes in mice after combination of UFP and AN exposure, providing new insight into the interplay between traffic noise and air pollution health risks.

title: FateDriver: Weakly supervised dual-view graph learning for transition-specific prioritization of candidate regulators in cellular reprogramming
abstract: Cellular reprogramming supports regenerative medicine, yet the endogenous regulators of a specified source-to-target transition remain incompletely defined. Existing computational methods rank candidate regulators from network topology, trajectory dynamics, or cell-state labels, leaving unused the factors experimentally delivered to induce the transition. We present Fat-eDriver, a weakly supervised dual-view graph neural network that jointly represents cells and genes from single-cell transcriptomes, treats the delivered factors as sparse gene-level labels, and ranks the remaining genes for a…

title: Homoharringtonine targets XPC to inhibit DNA damage repair and sensitize tumors to platinum-based chemotherapy
abstract: DNA damage repair (DDR) is essential for preserving genomic stability and also represents a key targetable axis in cancer drug development. Here, we identify and validate homoharringtonine (HHT), a clinically approved antileukemic drug, as a novel DDR inhibitor using a phenotype-driven, high-content screen based on 53BP1 Tudor-domain foci formation. Mechanistically, HHT directly binds XPC, a critical nucleotide excision repair (NER) factor, with high affinity (Kd = 158.4 nM) in a manner dependent on Thr795 of XPC.

title: Reversible Ferroelastic Strain Engineering Enables Stabilization of a Hidden Ga2O3 Polymorph
abstract: Understanding the formation, transformation, and stabilization of metastable polymorphs in functional compounds is a central challenge in materials science and has a profound impact on phase engineering and property control. Ga2O3 is an ultrawide bandgap semiconductor whose rich polymorphism underpins diverse electronic and optoelectronic functionalities, motivating continued exploration of its metastable phases.

title: Synthetic MRI from radiotherapy planning CT images for Head-and-Neck Cancer
abstract: BackgroundComputed Tomography (CT) provides geometric accuracy and electron density information essential for radiotherapy planning; however, it offers limited soft-tissue contrast. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) improves tumor visualization but introduces registration uncertainties when acquired separately from the radiotherapy planning CT (pCT). Cross-modality image synthesis enables the generation of synthetic MRI (sMRI) directly from pCT and may combine the strengths of both modalities, reducing reliance on MRI access.PurposeWe propose a two-stage deep-learning framework for generating sMRI from pCT image-sets specifically in head-and-neck (H&N) cancers, providing soft-tissue contrast comparable to ground-truth MR images (gtMRI).MethodsThis study included 60 patient cases with H&N cancer treated with radical radiotherapy between March 2022 and April 2024 for model development (50 for training, 10 for validation), plus 10 additional cases, independent of the development cohort for testing. All patients underwent a standard, non-contrast pCT scan followed by an MRI acquired on a 3T Siemens MR simulator. Images were deformably-registered, yielding 10,000 matched CT-MRI slice-pairs for model training. The proposed model utilizes a two-stage architecture, a Pix2Pix conditional generative adversarial network (GAN) for coarse sMRI synthesis, followed by a conditional diffusion model for refinement. To test the model's robustness, 10 patient cases with both pCT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) were used to generate sMRI. Model performance was assessed using structural similarity index (SSIM), multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM), mean absolute error (MAE), and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). In addition, the geometric agreement of the primary (GTVp_70) and nodal (GTVn_70) gross tumor volumes delineated on sMRI vs. gtMRI was independently assessed by two radiation oncologists (ROs) using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD).ResultsThe average MS-SSIM, SSIM, MAE and PSNR for pCT-derived sMRI were 0.82 ± 0.02, 0.70 ± 0.03, 0.05 ± 0.01, and 20.42 ± 0.66 dB, respectively. The mean MS-SSIM and SSIM values for ceCT-derived sMRI were 0.02 lower than those for the corresponding pCT-to-sMRI metrics. For the contour-based evaluation, sMRI-derived GTV contours achieved a mean DSC of 0.56 and 0.60 for GTVp_70, and 0.72 and 0.74 for GTVn_70 across the two ROs, relative to gtMRI contours.ConclusionOur proof-of-concept study demonstrates the feasibility of pCT-derived sMRI for H&N cancers using a deep-learning framework. The model produces grayscale patterns and soft-tissue contrast that closely resemble the gtMRI.
venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

title: Interpretable Drug-Target Prediction via Geometric Alignment: A Linear Alternative to Deep Architectural Complexity
abstract: Designing selective kinase inhibitors is a multiobjective optimization problem constrained by the structural conservation of the human kinome, along with the lack of high-quality interaction data. Traditional deep learning methods often train complex neural networks directly on small datasets and fail to generalize to new chemical scaffolds. To this end, we present Geometric Manifold Alignment, a novel linear approach that shifts away from architectural complexity. We introduce Multi-View Linear Manifold (MVLM), which aligns the latent spaces of ChemBERTa (small molecules) and ESM-2 (protein sequences) into a shared geometric interaction space. We pretrain MVLM on the Universal Foundation Set of 473 923 high-confidence interactions, where binding affinity is represented as geometric proximity between drug and target embeddings. Achieving an AUROC of 0.936 on KIBA and 0.928 on Davis, MVLM establishes the new state-of-the-art on industry-standard benchmarks, outperforming existing methods (p < 0.001). In this work, interpretability is geometric where interaction scores are cosine similarities in a shared manifold, and the learned structure recovers kinase phylogenetic relationships without supervision. We also demonstrate the model's utility as a transparent discovery engine by retrieving known clinical targets of FDA-approved drugs. Our findings suggest that aligning pretrained chemical and biological representations provides a scalable and interpretable approach to advancing computational drug discovery.

title: Accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth via tensor decomposition
abstract: Phase-field models provide a powerful framework for simulating grain growth phenomena in polycrystalline materials, but their application to large-scale systems is limited by the high computational and memory costs associated with resolving multiple phase variables over fine spatial and temporal scales. This paper presents a tensor decomposition based model reduction framework for accelerating phase-field simulations of grain growth. The proposed method exploits the underlying low-rank structure of the evolving phase-field variables and represents the high-dimensional solution in a spatially decomposed tensor format. By performing the numerical computations directly within this reduced representation, the framework decreases storage requirements and reduces the cost of repeatedly solving the phase-field equations. The number of modes for the decomposed approximation is controlled during the online computation with a subspace mode-updating algorithm, to balance computational efficiency and approximation accuracy. The method is assessed using representative grain growth problems, and its predictions are compared with those obtained from conventional full-order finite element simulations. The results demonstrate that the formulation can accurately reproduce the evolution of grain morphology and the principal characteristics of grain growth kinetics while substantially improving computational efficiency. The proposed framework therefore provides a promising approach for extending phase-field simulations to larger spatial domains, finer discretizations, and systems containing a large number of phase variables.

title: Bounded Retained History in a Proxy Flow Replay: A Mixed Predictive Pilot and an Allocation Study
abstract: We examine bounded retained history through a frozen predictive pilot and a subsequent allocation study on a curated UNSW-NB15 flow mirror. Both use an artificial release-order replay based on raw ltime ticks, with equal-tick records querying a shared prior-group state. In the pilot, the model with added retained relational features had lower reconnaissance recall than the current-flow-plus-counters baseline (43.66% versus 47.84%) and lower benign false-positive rate (3.63% versus 6.68%) at separately frozen operating thresholds, together with lower AUROC. This mixed result did not establish a predictive advantage. A development-only audit subsequently found that capacity eviction dominated expiration in the 256-record, 300-tick FIFO state, with a median completed record lifetime of 11 ticks. A protocol specified before its single execution, but after the pilot and post-hoc mechanism audit, compared five label-blind retention arms on the already-used development trace. Its primary equal-source endpoint averaged retained/reference ratios for service-expanded source out-degree and source-destination service diversity. Source-balanced retention at 256 records exceeded FIFO-256 by a pooled endpoint difference of 0.440738 and met the prespecified materiality and subblock rule. Crucially, the event-weighted ratios for both quantities decreased relative to FIFO-256: the result is specific to the equal-source weighting objective and does not establish uniformly improved retention. The study supplies neither evidence of detection improvement nor an explanation of the pilot result. Reused data, concentrated reconnaissance support, proxy timing, and the absence of a qualified independent corpus bound the interpretation.

title: Theory of the charge response of the boron-vacancy spin in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride
abstract: The boron vacancy $V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$ in hexagonal boron nitride is a leading two-dimensional spin sensor, but the microscopic connection between nearby charge positions and its spin Hamiltonian remains poorly understood. Calculations for carbon and oxygen donors 3.85--8.08 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ away show that direction matters, not only distance. In the frozen lattice, reversing a carbon donor's azimuth at 4.35 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$ (C1 to C1m) more than halves $|E|$ and turns its axis across the mirror line. The ratio is 0.467 with the Perdew--Burke--Ernzerhof (PBE) functional, against 1 for distance alone. A field-plus-gradient model fitted to six donor configurations, including C1 but excluding C1m, predicted a ratio of 0.443 before C1m was calculated. Heyd--Scuseria--Ernzerhof hybrid statics give 0.432 and PBE relaxation 0.600. Exploratory analysis suggests why direction matters: a charge's potential differs at the three vacancy nitrogens and moves the spin of the two $e'$ holes among them, more when the charge faces one nitrogen than the gap between two. $E$ follows this spin imbalance through one constant, $c\approx8$ GHz per $μ_{\mathrm{B}}$, across donors and applied fields, whereas in PBE $D$ is nearly insensitive to it. A three-site model with one fitted screening constant reproduces the frozen-lattice $E$ to 83 MHz rms. Results are for one charge state in a free-standing monolayer; absolute $|E|$ varies by tens of percent across approximations.

title: Beyond Unit-Circle Eigenvalues: Invariant Bases for Stable State Space Dynamics
abstract: Diagonal state space models process long sequences at linear cost, yet the same transition is applied at every step of a rollout, so an unconstrained recurrence holds no quantity fixed and the state decays or grows without bound. Current designs constrain one quantity, and preserving one does not guarantee preservation of the others, so a model can hold its norm to machine precision while momentum drifts by hundreds of percent. We claim that the conserved quantities of a diagonal recurrence are layered, that each layer requires a strictly stronger condition on the operator, and that a unit-modulus spectrum reaches only the outermost. Acting on the claim, we enforce the conditions required for every layer by construction. The generator of the Kronecker-Cayley transition (KC) is a graph Laplacian over object subspaces, $\mathbf{H}=\mathbf{L}\otimes I_m$, advanced by a Cayley transform, and the step stays diagonal at $O(N^3+N^2m)$ cost. The conserved set is exactly a $2m^2$-dimensional family of quadratic forms, held at every parameter value, so the quantities and the dynamics the construction reaches are fixed before training. On four conservation benchmarks, KC holds total mass at or near the reference floor while every diagonal baseline loses it by orders of magnitude. We further compare against mass correction and find that two correctors fail once the underlying prediction diverges, which shows that assembly rather than correction is necessary for a guarantee that holds across the rollout. A free modal basis trained under a conservation penalty conserves only by freezing its spectrum, whereas the assembled operator conserves with every mode but one free to rotate. Beyond these benchmarks, KC holds the linear momentum of three $N$-body systems and, at the operator level, the conserved quantity in molecular dynamics, chemical kinetics, pharmacokinetics and power-grid swing dynamics.

title: Restrained Diffusion Bridges: Targeted Denoiser Training and Refinement
abstract: Diffusion models are often inaccurate in critical, data-sparse regions of the target distribution. Sampling from restrained distributions, biased distributions used in classical enhanced sampling to concentrate data near chosen configurations, can control where training data are collected but biases the learned distribution. We establish that this bias cancels exactly when forward noising from restrained data is conditioned on the restrained configuration at an appropriately chosen intermediate time. This allows a pretrained model fine-tuned on restrained data to achieve high accuracy in any chosen region of the target distribution, regardless of its probability, using standard denoising or flow matching objectives without importance weights. When no target data are available, Gibbs sampling enables inference from a model trained exclusively on restrained data.

title: ADInteractome: discovering Alzheimer's disease-associated gene interactions from single-nucleus RNA-seq data through neural interaction states
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder characterized by amyloid $\beta $ plaques and tau tangles, yet its molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Advances in single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) have provided profound insights into the cellular heterogeneity of AD-associated brains. In this study, we introduce ADInteractome, an interpretable artificial intelligence framework designed to discover gene interactions associated with AD directly from the internal state of neural networks trained on the snRNA-seq data of brain cells. The method is based on the intuition that if a neural network can accurately classify cells from AD and non-AD donors based on their snRNA-seq data, then its internal interaction states, reflecting interaction patterns within the gene expression data, are informative for identifying biologically meaningful gene interactions. Applied to a large-scale snRNA-seq dataset from the Seattle Alzheimer's Disease Brain Cell Atlas, ADInteractome reveals cell-type-specific and AD-associated gene circuits supported by existing literature. The results were further supported by our virtual knock-out and knock-in experiments, a novel concept to probe our findings through a data-driven approach. Compared with traditional co-expression network methods, it achieves stronger enrichment for known AD-associated gene interactions and uncovers novel interaction patterns. These findings highlight the potential of interpretable AI approaches for elucidating complex molecular interactions in neurodegenerative disease.

title: Low-pass filtering revisited: ramped phase randomization for cryo-EM map comparison and data augmentation
abstract: Conventional low-pass filters attenuate or remove high-frequency Fourier amplitudes but leave the phases intact wherever the amplitude response stays above zero. As a result, fine-scale detail of the original signal can persist beyond the target resolution. A sharp cutoff removes this detail but produces ringing artifacts. To address both limitations, this work introduces ramped phase randomization, which extends a conventional low-pass filter by adding random offsets to Fourier phases that increase smoothly with spatial frequency. For cryo-EM maps, the correlation between a map at the target resolution and an ideal, noiseless map sets the levels of the phase offsets, with a correction for the finite resolution of the input map. On three published map pairs, ramped phase filtering reduced the higher resolution parent's fine detail to a level similar to that of independently determined maps at the lower target resolution, whereas amplitude-only filtering kept the parent's sharp features. The FSCs between the filtered maps and their parents closely resembled those of the experimental maps. The same filter also serves as a data augmentation approach for neural network-based machine learning. With ramped phase randomization, each augmented copy keeps the power spectrum and low-frequency content of the original example but has a different high-frequency pattern. For simulated CryoBench particles of 16 ribosome assembly states, phase augmentation raised mean test accuracy in all 20 combinations of training-set size and latent dimension, by 20.8 percentage points on average (range from 3.3 points to 44.2 points). On two general deep learning benchmarks, mean test accuracy rose from 92.15% to 96.99% with 60 labelled UCI Synthetic Control traces and from 53.44% to 74.27% with 500 labelled noisy MNIST images. The ramped phase randomization is implemented in an open-source Python package, with a companion browser application for interactive visualization of cryo-EM maps and filtering effects.

title: Controlling the Sign and Magnitude of the Thermoreflectance Coefficient of Gold-MoS$_2$ Metamaterials
abstract: Heating a material changes how much light it reflects. This effect, quantified by the thermoreflectance coefficient $C_\mathrm{TR}$, enables temperature sensing, while it is a nuisance for situations where constant reflection is crucial. Whereas temperature detection requires a large $C_\mathrm{TR}$, the latter situation demands it to be as close to zero as possible. Controlling the $C_\mathrm{TR}$ has so far relied on the selection of materials and wavelengths, rather than engineering the coefficient itself. This work demonstrates that the $C_\mathrm{TR}$ of a 50 nm thin gold film on SiO$_2$/Si can be controlled in sign and magnitude by an ultrathin ($<$8 nm) MoS$_2$ film underneath it. Time-resolved thermoreflectance measurements reveal suppression, sign inversion, and revival of the thermoreflectance signal, controlled by three knobs: ($i$) the buried MoS$_2$ thickness, ($ii$) probe wavelength, and ($iii$) ambient temperature. Transfer-matrix simulations using temperature-dependent dielectric functions of gold and MoS$_2$ reproduce all experimental observations, demonstrating an optothermal metamaterial platform with controllable properties. In particular, these (anti-)thermoreflective metamaterial mirrors bring $C_\mathrm{TR}$ under the same interference design rules previously applied to the optical response itself, opening ways to maximize or minimize the temperature dependence of the optical reflectance, tailored to the specific application.

title: Valence-Selective Electrophoretic Transport in Neutral Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: Understanding how confinement alters the transport of charged molecules is central to the advancement of separation, energy, and sensing technologies. Polyamines are small, linear molecules with ionizable groups, making them an ideal model for investigating charge transport in confinement beyond monatomic ions. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we investigate how molecular length, net charge, and charge placement affect the electrophoretic transport of polyamines through single-walled carbon nanotubes (CNTs). We find that nanometer-scale confinement reverses the mobility ordering observed in free solution -- in a CNT of radius 0.68 nm, spermine (q = +4) travels more slowly than ethylamine (q = +1), contrasting with the expected scaling of mobility with valence in bulk. Further, we find that mobility decreases faster than the inverse of valence, though molecular size and length vary alongside this trend. Comparisons of doubly protonated spermidine microspecies reveal the additional influence of charge placement at fixed net valence. Upon moving one proton of dicationic spermidine from the central to a terminal nitrogen, the mobility is increased by 42%. We analyze hydration structure and solute-solvent association, identifying local-solvation differences between protonation topologies that accompany these distinct transport responses under confinement. These results suggest that neutral CNTs could support valence-selective nanofluidic transport, with additional sensitivity to molecular structure and protonation topology.

title: Unoccupied spin texture of ordered Bi films on vicinal Ge substrates
abstract: Vicinal surfaces offer a compelling testing ground in surface science: breaking the high symmetry of a singular surface introduces periodic step arrays that can modify surface states on the terraces and influence epitaxial ordering; the interplay between these effects governs morphology and electronic structure, especially in heavy, spin--orbit-coupled materials. We combine low-energy electron diffraction (LEED) and spin-polarized inverse photoemission (SP-IPES) with ab-initio calculations for the Bi$(1\,1\,1)$ reference, for the first time on a true high-index vicinal bismuth surface. On the ordered Bi$(9\,9\,11)$ vicinal film selected by Ge$(2\,2\,3)$, the measured unoccupied-state spin-sign sequence matches the calculated initial-state spectral function of Bi$(1\,1\,1)$ terraces. Conversely, the pseudo-cubic Bi domains retained on Ge$(4\,4\,3)$ and Ge$(3\,3\,1)$ exhibit a characteristic spin-polarized surface-state response referenced to the macroscopic vicinal surface. These results show that the substrate cut selects not only the morphology of the Bi film, but also the crystallographic reference frame of its unoccupied spin texture.

title: Rational Design of Highly Fluorescent N-Doped Carbon Nanoparticles for Hg2+ Ion Sensing via Machine Learning and Computational Analysis
abstract: A novel fluorescent sensor was developed using diphenylcarbazone-ligand-functionalized carbon nanoparticles for Hg2+ ion detection. The carbon nanoparticles were synthesized by the hydrothermal method using vitamin C as the carbon source and functionalized with an Hg2+ ion-selective diphenylcarbazone organic ligand via a Schiff base reaction. The as-synthesized carbon nanoparticles exhibited excellent water solubility, a uniform size of 10-12 nm, and a fluorescence quantum yield of 8.4%.
venue: Langmuir : the ACS journal of surfaces and colloids

title: Quantum Control of Molecular Photodissociation Reactions with Intense Laser Fields
abstract: Quantum control of molecular reaction dynamics has been a challenging subject of research for many years. Here, a new control scheme is proposed to modify the fragment distributions of molecular photodissociation reactions. The scheme is applied to the A-band photolysis of CH3I, which is simulated using a realistic wave packet model. The control scheme applies a single moderately intense (1010–1013 W cm–2) pump pulse to excite CH3I. This pulse produces light-induced conical intersections (LICIs) between the ground and excited electronic states, that reshape the natural diabatic potentials, generating new adiabatic light-induced potentials (LIPs). The new LIPs lead to different photodissociation dynamics, producing different fragment distributions compared to the weak-field regime. Complete inversion of the branching ratio I*(2P1/2)/I(2P3/2) between the two dissociation channels is achieved, with the previously dominant I*(2P1/2) channel practically suppressed, and the minor I(2P3/2) channel becoming the dominant one. Experimental implementation of the scheme appears straightforward and of universal application to photodissociation processes.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Physics-Based AI-Augmented Workflows Discovering Candidate Graphene Quantum Dot Near-Infrared Chromophores
abstract: Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) exhibit optical properties that depend strongly on their size, edge structure, and surface functionalization, but identifying the molecular structures responsible for near-infrared (NIR) emission remains challenging because of their structural complexity and disorder. In this work, we developed a computational framework combining rule-based molecular generation, semi-empirical quantum chemistry calculations, machine learning, and time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) to predict possible chemically realistic candidate GQDs with NIR-emitting optical properties. A fusion-based hexagonal lattice growth approach was used to generate 100,000 candidate graphitic structures. A random subset of 5000 structures was selected for semiempirical calculations. Computed band gaps were used to train and evaluate five machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, and Neural Network). LightGBM predicted bandgaps were used to pre-screen the remaining 95,000 structures. 11,000 structures with low predicted gaps were selected for semiempirical calculations, and 50 top candidates with low gap and low SA score were selected for TD-DFT calculations employing LC-ωPBE functional. All 50 structures were predicted to exhibit NIR emission, offering a computed database of candidate NIR-emitting GQDs for future validation against experiment.

title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
abstract: Refractory compositionally complex alloys (R-CCAs) show great promise as next generation structural materials for extreme conditions, but alloys with excellent high temperature mechanical properties most often exhibit virtually zero room temperature tensile ductility, hindering potential commercial application. Several semi-empirical metrics have been employed for predicting plasticity in R-CCAs, including valence electron concentration, Pugh ratio, Rice criteria, and the D-parameter. While many currently available ductility metrics correlate very well when compressive plasticity is considered, only the density functional theory (DFT) based D-parameter shows a strong correlation in tension. A new ductility metric is developed using CALculation of PHAse Diagrams (CALPHAD) thermodynamics, Gamma, with includes the free energy difference between the body-centered cubic (BCC) and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) phases, the interfacial free energy of a (110) BCC surface, and an electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion. The Gamma parameter exhibits better correlation with tensile ductility than D-parameter and performs equally well in compression. While this improvement is modest, a thermodynamically grounded ductility metric is clearly required to capture intrinsic ductility behavior. Extrinsic contributions to brittle behavior in R-CCAs, namely interstitial oxygen content, are also briefly discussed. Combining the Gamma ductility parameter with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility is proposed as a first order attempt to capture both intrinsic and extrinsic contributions to ductile behavior in R-CCAs.

title: ZeroGraph: Compositional Blockwise Training via Materialized Boundary Supervision
abstract: Blockwise learning can remove online gradient dependencies across depth, but independently optimized blocks need not compose into a useful model. We present ZeroGraph, a systems transformation for pretrained-model conversion and distillation that materializes a frozen teacher's coherent boundary trajectory as a versioned dataset. Each partition then trains with disjoint parameters, optimizer state, random state, and checkpoints, replacing live cross-depth dependencies with persistent supervision. Experiments separate learning quality from systems behavior. On GPT-2 Large, an unanchored objective reduces denoising error by 99.44%, yet assembled held-out cross-entropy worsens from 3.63 to 10.48 and context use becomes negative. A six-arm TinyLlama study identifies clean teacher-boundary regression as the successful interface; the tested noisy objective fails with cached or online targets. The clean recipe passes quality and context-use gates across three Qwen2.5-1.5B seeds and on a 3.086B Qwen2.5 model. In an objective-matched comparison, cached and online targets are bitwise identical. Cached jobs are faster after materialization, but a 618.31 s cache-build cost prevents wall-time break-even through 16 measured reuses. Boundary-shift tests show tolerance to intermediate representation mismatch, and an interrupted block resumes to a bitwise-identical final state without rerunning unaffected blocks. In the tested pretrained-model conversion and distillation setting, cross-depth semantic dependence can move from online optimization into persistent data.

title: Ferroelectric Switching in x-cut MgO-doped Thin-Film Lithium Niobate: Implications for Periodic Poling and Domain-Wall Electronics
abstract: Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) revives a mature ferroelectric as a wafer-scale platform for integrated photonics and, increasingly, for domain-wall electronics such as nonvolatile memories and memristors. Both applications rely on controlled ferroelectric switching, which is poorly understood in TFLN: periodic poling consistently requires electric fields above 30~kV/mm, far above the coercive fields of about 21~kV/mm and 4.5~kV/mm of bulk congruent and 5~mol\% MgO-doped lithium niobate, respectively. Here, we present systematic ferroelectric hysteresis measurements on x-cut, 5~mol\% MgO-doped TFLN with coplanar electrodes as used for periodic poling, combining the positive-up-negative-down (PUND) method with second-harmonic microscopy (SHM). We obtain a spontaneous polarization of $(0.72\pm0.02)$~C/m$^2$, consistent with bulk values, while the coercive field varies between 24 and 40~kV/mm with the voltage ramp rate and depends on the electrode geometry. We identify three contributions to the high coercive fields: (i) fast voltage ramps, (ii) finger electrodes, and (iii) the coplanar surface-electrode geometry. Together with bulk data, the coercive field follows a single power law of the ramp rate over five orders of magnitude, showing that the high fields are dominated by switching dynamics rather than by intrinsic thin-film properties. Moreover, the apparent internal field depends on the electrode geometry, and reverse switching leaves buried, electrically isolated domains. These results provide guidelines for scalable, fab-compatible periodic poling---one of the principal bottlenecks of TFLN device integration---and for the write and erase operation of TFLN domain-wall devices.

title: Modeling and Experimental Validation of Bubble-Induced Performance Losses in Microstructured Copper Electrodes for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
abstract: Water electrolysis is a promising technology for sustainable hydrogen (H$_2$) production. However, gas bubble formation significantly degrades the electrochemical surface area ($A_{\rm EC}$) and the electrocatalytic activity of microstructured electrodes in water electrolyzer cells. Existing theoretical models fail to connect computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and electrochemistry to analyze how bubble dynamics affect the performance of gas-evolving microstructured electrodes. This work develops a multiphysics-based theoretical model that couples two-phase CFD with Butler-Volmer and Faradaic kinetics, incorporating exchange current density, cell current, gravitational acceleration, surface tension, and fluid properties such as density and viscosity. The model quantifies essential electrochemical parameters, such as the enhancement in $A_{\rm EC}$ and the overpotential ($η$), which deviate by less than 7\% and 15\%, respectively, from the experimental results. Evaluations of the fabricated microstructured electrodes using polarization curves, cyclic voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, and linear polarization resistance techniques demonstrate reduced $η$ by 2.49--21.39\% and 9.55--24.32\% for oxygen (O$_2$) and H$_2$ evolution, respectively. Furthermore, the model reveals the interplay between enhanced geometric surface area and bubble-transport limitations, facilitating the optimization and analysis of structural parameters. These findings establish a physics-informed roadmap for designing optimal, robust, and industry-scalable microstructured electrodes for efficient H$_2$ generation via water electrolysis.

title: Band Alignment of Grafted versus Directly Bonded Si/Ge Heterostructures
abstract: The electronic properties of semiconductor heterostructures are influenced by the local bonding and electrostatic environment at the heterointerface. Here, we investigate how the interface-formation mechanism modifies the band alignment of Si/Ge heterostructures by directly comparing Al2O3-mediated semiconductor grafting with direct bonding. Interface-sensitive X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy combined with Kraut analysis reveals type-I band alignment for both structures, but with different band offsets: the valence-band offset increases from ~0.08 eV for directly bonded Si/Ge to ~0.21 eV for grafted Si/Al2O3/Ge, accompanied by a corresponding reduction in the conduction-band offset. Raman spectroscopy further distinguishes the two interfacial configurations. The different core-level shifts and band offsets indicate that the electronic structure is sensitive to the interfacial bonding and electrostatic environment introduced by the two integration schemes. These results demonstrate that, even for an identical Si/Ge material pair, the interface-formation pathway provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling heterojunction band alignment, offering a route toward interface-engineered electronic and optoelectronic devices.

title: Chirality-Induced Angular-Momentum Pumping by Moving Charges
abstract: Chirality-induced spin selectivity is established even in light elements at room temperature; dissipation and electron correlations are implicated, here combined in one mechanism. Injected electron wave packets coherently radiate chiral phonons; electronic absorption competing with phonon decay sets the fraction electrons receive and its temperature dependence. Spin-orbit coupling itself is not renormalized; it becomes effectively large because both the orbital and spin moments it couples are enhanced by Coulomb correlations.

title: Atom-Wise Allocation of Message-Passing Scale for Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: Molecular properties depend on chemical structure at different ranges, from local polar groups governing solvation to extended substructures shaping bioactivity, yet graph neural networks usually fix one propagation scale for every atom. We present PRISM (Per-atom Routing over Intermediate States of Message Passing), in which each atom's encoded features produce a bounded scalar that positions a unimodal distribution over retained message-passing states and matching circular-fingerprint radii. Because one coordinate translates the whole profile, allocated depth responds to the routing scalar in closed form: at fixed temperature it is nondecreasing, its sensitivity scales with the profile variance, and it saturates in the clipped regions. Beyond providing closed-form analyzability, this constrained one-parameter profile matches or significantly outperforms parameter-matched, unconstrained node-wise gates and Jumping Knowledge attention. Under scaffold partitions with equal tuning budgets against eight graph, fingerprint, and geometric baselines, PRISM trained from scratch without three-dimensional coordinates achieves the lowest mean error on aqueous solubility and hydration free energy and strong accuracy on BACE and BBBP. As a general layer-combination rule, PRISM transfers directly to GCN, GIN, and GAT backbones, reducing hydration free energy error by up to 29% relative to last-layer readout. Applied to a pre-trained GIN, it improves on last-layer readout on four of six endpoints and gives the lowest lipophilicity error overall. In trained models, allocated depth differs systematically between atom types in a task-dependent way, and permuting profiles among a molecule's atoms raises prediction error on several endpoints, so the rule acts as a learned counterpart of atom typing.

title: Data-Scarce, Multi-Granular, Multimodal: Benchmark Design for Biosynthetic Gene Clusters
abstract: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) are co-located genes that encode the biosynthesis of specialized metabolites, an important source of antibiotics, anticancer agents, immunosuppressants, and agricultural bioactives. Deep learning, particularly self-supervised foundation models, has spurred interest in BGC sequence modeling, but evaluation has lagged behind: existing benchmarks often rely on coarse classification over small curated datasets, providing limited discrimination among models and insight into downstream utility. We propose a benchmark-design framework in which an informative benchmark should be discriminative, separating models with statistical confidence, and applicable, spanning scientifically meaningful tasks under different levels of generalization. We instantiate this framework as BGC-Bench, which derives five tasks from MIBiG, ranging from A-domain substrate prediction to BGC-molecule retrieval, evaluates them under genotype- and phenotype-shift splits, includes an active-learning setting for label-scarce discovery, and is easily extensible to new tasks and encoders. BGCs further provide a shared testbed across granularities and modalities: BGC-Bench compares twelve encoders on nucleotide, amino-acid, or Pfam-domain sequences, including compositional baselines for each input type, and combines BGC and chemical encoders for cross-modal retrieval. No single representation dominates: the best granularity depends on the biological scale of the task, and pretrained encoders do not consistently outperform other representations across tasks and splits. Active-learning experiments show that most tasks remain data-limited, encoder rankings change with labeling budget, and acquisition strategies yield modest gains. These results show that BGC model evaluation requires task-diverse, shift-aware benchmarks, and the framework can be generalized to benchmark design beyond BGCs.

title: The Cryptocurrency Trend Factor Revisited: Predictive Information, Portfolio Construction, and Pricing Claims
abstract: We reassess five economic claims about the cryptocurrency trend factor (CTREND): cross-sectional return predictability, high risk-adjusted performance, incremental information beyond market, size, and momentum, the ability to replace momentum in factor models, and robustness among large and liquid coins and after trading costs. Our reconstruction and code audit identify issues in information timing, technical indicators, forecast coverage, portfolio formation, and return accounting. We first correct future-information use and related settlement rules, then implement broader corrections to indicators, forecast availability, and portfolio accounting. Without additional coin exclusions, the first stage changes CTREND's mean weekly gross return from 4.07% to 4.25%, annualized Sharpe ratio from 2.08 to 1.48, and weekly alpha relative to published market, size, and momentum factors from 2.77% to 3.06%. After comprehensive correction, these become 0.05%, 0.01, and -1.38%; the alpha is no longer significant. Replacing momentum with CTREND yields an advantage in maximum squared Sharpe ratios of 0.058 in the original implementation, 0.024 after the first-stage correction, and -0.0185 after comprehensive correction, with a statistically significant overall decline. Mean weekly gross returns for the largest 100 coins change from 2.93% to 3.99% to 1.00%, while mean weekly net returns for the full long-short portfolio under the lowest assumed trading costs change from 2.93% to 3.35% to -0.87%. These findings show that reported performance and factor-substitution gains depend materially on implementation and sample composition. We distinguish predictive information, an independent return premium, and the incremental value of replacing an existing factor as separate economic claims.

title: Can Large Language Model Agents Learn by Watching Tutorial Videos?
abstract: Humans continuously acquire knowledge from carefully crafted materials such as books and tutorial videos, carrying that understanding into future tasks. Millions of such instructional videos are uploaded online every day, yet LLM agents remain unable to exploit this ever-expanding wealth of human teaching. Their capabilities are frozen after training, while parameter updates at scale remain prohibitively expensive. This raises the central question: can LLM agents learn from this vast instructional resource without parameter updates? We introduce Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL), a nonparametric continual-learning paradigm that consolidates tutorial videos into a persistent, structured tutorialbook memory through a two-stage adversarial process that harvests hard, video-grounded questions and uses them to refine the memory. At inference time, TAL retrieves through a Table-of-Contents (TOC) tree, tying retrieval directly to the model's reasoning rather than to embedding similarity. To study this setting, we introduce VidLearn, a multimodal QA benchmark built from 72 chess tutorial videos spanning 12 openings. On VidLearn, TAL outperforms all evaluated baselines and improves monotonically as more videos are consumed, achieving up to 113% and 91% relative gains over the corresponding vanilla MLLMs on the training and test splits, respectively. In actual gameplay, TAL reaches a stronger opening-phase position than its vanilla counterpart in 69% of head-to-head games. Evaluation in a second domain further demonstrates the generality of TAL. Together, these results highlight instructional videos as a scalable resource for parameter-update-free agent continual learning.

title: Learning materials spectra across modalities and scales with structure-conditioned neural fields
abstract: Spectroscopic observables encode rich information about material behavior across diverse, often high-dimensional domains of energy, momentum, and other experimental coordinates, providing critical insights into the physical properties underlying material functionalities and applications. However, learning these responses directly from atomic structures remains challenging due to the complexity of both structural configurations and spectroscopic observation spaces. Here, we develop a structure-conditioned neural-field framework that learns continuous spectroscopic response functions by coupling an equivariant structural encoder with a coordinate-conditioned network. The framework accurately predicts spectroscopic observables across diverse observation domains, ranging from one-dimensional densities of states to multidimensional scattering functions. We show that fine-tuning with limited spectral supervision captures strain- and composition-dependent spectral changes, with validated transfer to alloy configurations containing hundreds of atoms and computational scalability demonstrated for configurations exceeding $10^4$ atoms. Our work establishes a versatile and computationally scalable approach to learning structure-spectroscopy relationships, providing a foundation for spectroscopic analysis and future materials characterization, inverse problems, and experimental design.

title: Energy Transfer and Strong Coupling in Plasmonic Systems
abstract: The coupling between plasmon resonances of metal nanostructures and electronic excitations of molecular/semiconductor systems is important in a number of applications, including surface enhanced spectroscopy, hot-electron catalysis, plasmon-induced resonance energy transfer and the creation of hybrid light-matter states. The past several decades has seen a large number of experimental studies of these effects, as well as the development of theory to explain the results. In this Perspectives article we use classical electromagnetic (EM) simulations to examine how the localized surface plasmon resonances (LSPRs) of metal nanoparticles and propagating surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) in extended metal nanostructures (wires/plates/films) are affected by interactions with a molecular/semiconductor system. The classical EM simulations are complemented by a quantum model for plasmon-exciton coupling based on the macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED) framework, along with Holstein vibrations. The goals are to show how LSPR spectra and SPP dispersion curves/attenuation constants changes as the strength of the molecular/semiconductor electronic transition increases and the system evolves from an energy transfer limit to strong coupling, and to provide an understanding of the decay processes from both classical EM and MQED perspectives.

title: GenMAS: A Machine Learning-Based Modeling and Assessment Strategy for ADMET Profiling and its Application in PBPK Simulation
abstract: Evaluation of pharmacokinetic (PK) properties is crucial for the discovery of high-quality drug candidates while minimizing unnecessary biological and clinical trial costs. Compared with in vitro and in vivo studies, in silico methods offer a faster and more cost-efficient alternative. However, despite advances in computational approaches, accurate PK assessment and simulation remain challenging. Current industrial applications are often hindered by a heavy reliance on animal data, limited flexibility, and insufficient project-specific customization.
